post: People read statements and rated how likely each was to be true. Each statement had the same content but was written either in concrete language or in abstract language. People judged the concrete wording as more likely to be true.

claim: Those made to feel low in status showed a trend toward a stronger automatic preference for the calorie-packed foods than those made to feel high.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
post: People were put in a situation that made them feel either lower or higher in social standing compared with others. Then they did a task that measured their automatic, gut-level liking for calorie-packed foods versus fruits and vegetables. Those made to feel low in status showed a trend toward a stronger automatic preference for the calorie-packed foods than those made to feel high.

claim: People felt more empathy when the lamb was shown as a living animal.
method: 187 participants viewed an advertisement for lamb in which the animal was presented either as a living animal or as meat, then reported their empathy.
post: People viewed an advertisement for lamb. In one version the lamb was shown as a living animal, and in the other as meat. Then they reported how much empathy they felt. People felt more empathy when the lamb was shown as a living animal.

claim: People remembered the details they had not discussed better than the details they had.
method: 40 participants watched a film with a co-witness who saw a different version, discussed the film together, then individually recalled details.
post: Pairs of people watched a film, each seeing a different version, and then discussed it. Afterwards each person recalled details alone. People remembered the details they had not discussed better than the details they had.

claim: The turn-taking games gave the two sides higher payoffs.
method: 158 participants in an experimental arbitration selection game chose arbitrators under either a simultaneous veto-rank procedure or a sequential shortlisting procedure, and their payoffs were compared.
post: In a game, two sides had to pick a judge for a dispute. In some games both sides struck out names at the same time. In others they took turns narrowing down a list. The turn-taking games gave the two sides higher payoffs.

claim: People near the hand sanitizer reported more politically conservative attitudes.
method: 52 people in a public setting reported their political attitudes either in the presence of a hand-sanitizer dispenser or in a control condition.
post: People in a public place reported their political attitudes. For some, a hand-sanitizer dispenser was nearby, and for others it was not. People near the hand sanitizer reported more politically conservative attitudes.

claim: People who had taken part disliked the person who refused, but people who had only watched did not.
method: Participants took part in a racist task or merely observed it, then rated a person who refused to go along and an obedient person.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
post: Some people took part in a racist task and others only watched it. Then they rated a person who refused to go along with it. People who had taken part disliked the person who refused, but people who had only watched did not.

claim: At times when they were most likely to conceive, they favored single, masculine men.
method: 208 women rated the attractiveness of men described as single or attached, with conception risk estimated from menstrual cycle phase.
post: Women rated how attractive they found men who were described as either single or already in a relationship. Women who already had a partner favored the attached men at times in their cycle when they were least likely to conceive. At times when they were most likely to conceive, they favored single, masculine men.

claim: Fewer people looked at the cost when it was observable (59%) than when it was hidden (70%).
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
post: People played a money game where they could cooperate with another player. They could choose whether to see exactly what cooperating would cost them. For some, others could see whether they looked; for others, it stayed hidden. Fewer people looked at the cost when it was observable (59%) than when it was hidden (70%).

claim: People expected more corruption in the organization with more bosses over workers.
method: 97 people read about an organization with either many or few levels of bosses, then rated how much corruption they expected from its employees.
journal: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
post: People read about an organization that had either many levels of bosses or few. Then they rated how much corruption they expected from its employees. People expected more corruption in the organization with more bosses over workers.

claim: Trump supporters were more likely than other people to wrongly pick Trump's crowd.
method: 651 survey respondents viewed photos of the 2017 Trump and 2009 Obama inauguration crowds and selected which showed a larger crowd.
post: People saw photos of the crowds at the 2017 Trump inauguration and the 2009 Obama inauguration and picked which crowd was larger. Trump supporters were more likely than other people to wrongly pick Trump's crowd.

claim: The people with the wider mix said they felt better about their lives.
method: 576 US adults completed a preregistered survey reporting their social interactions and well-being; the diversity of relationship types in their social portfolios was compared with their well-being, controlling for total amount of social interaction.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
post: Adults listed who they spent each part of yesterday with. Some had spent time with a wide mix of people, such as a partner, friends, coworkers and family, and others with fewer kinds of people. The people with the wider mix said they felt better about their lives.

claim: White female leaders were given lower status when they acted dominant rather than communal, but Black female leaders were not.
method: 84 participants evaluated leaders who expressed dominance or communality, with leader race and gender varied.
post: People evaluated leaders who acted either dominant or communal. The leaders were Black or White, women or men. White female leaders were given lower status when they acted dominant rather than communal, but Black female leaders were not.

claim: Quick immoral decisions made the person look worse than slow ones, and quick moral decisions made the person look better than slow ones.
method: 119 participants read about a person making a moral or immoral decision either quickly or slowly, then rated the person's moral character.
post: People read about someone making a moral or an immoral decision, either quickly or slowly. Then they rated the person's moral character. Quick immoral decisions made the person look worse than slow ones, and quick moral decisions made the person look better than slow ones.

claim: People who saw the vegetables as scarce chose a bigger share of their favorite than people who saw them as plentiful.
method: 200 people rated how much they liked four vegetables, then rated the supply of each as scarce or abundant, and chose six pieces from the set.
post: People rated how much they liked four vegetables. Then some were led to think the vegetables were scarce and others plentiful, and everyone chose six pieces from the set. People who saw the vegetables as scarce chose a bigger share of their favorite than people who saw them as plentiful.

claim: Later people liked the object paired with positive items more, though they did not remember the pairings.
method: 50 participants viewed several hundred words and images, some of which repeatedly paired novel objects with positive or negative items, then rated the objects.
post: People were told a study was about vigilance and watched several hundred words and images go by. Mixed in, one unfamiliar object kept appearing with positive items and another with negative ones. Later people liked the object paired with positive items more, though they did not remember the pairings.

claim: People from the harsh places were judged as more impulsive and short-sighted, whether rich or poor.
method: 96 participants rated people described as coming from desperate or hopeful ecologies on five life history strategy traits, with wealth information varied.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
post: People read about someone from a harsh, unpredictable place or from a secure, stable one, rich or poor. Then they guessed how impulsive and short-sighted that person was. People from the harsh places were judged as more impulsive and short-sighted, whether rich or poor.

claim: The people who weren't busy moved their estimates further away from the starting number.
method: 94 participants made numerical estimates after generating their own starting values; some were kept mentally busy while adjusting.
post: People made number estimates, starting from a number they had come up with themselves. Some were kept mentally busy while they adjusted their guess. The people who weren't busy moved their estimates further away from the starting number.

claim: Rats trained with delayed rewards chose the larger, later reward more often than rats trained with immediate rewards or no training.
method: 51 male Wistar rats received extended training with delayed reinforcers, immediate reinforcers, or no training, then chose between a smaller immediate reward and a larger delayed reward.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
post: Rats were trained with delayed rewards, with immediate rewards, or not at all. Then they chose between a smaller immediate reward and a larger delayed one. Rats trained with delayed rewards chose the larger, later reward more often than rats trained with immediate rewards or no training.

claim: They made more errors when the target appeared where the word's object usually is than when it appeared in the opposite place.
method: 18 participants saw an object word (e.g., head, foot) followed by a visual target presented at the top or bottom of the display, and identified the target.
post: People saw a word for something usually up high, like head, or down low, like foot. Then they tried to identify a target that appeared at the top or the bottom of the screen. They made more errors when the target appeared where the word's object usually is than when it appeared in the opposite place.

claim: Students who wrote about their own death liked the author who praised the country more than the one who criticized it.
method: 58 American students wrote about their own death or about watching television, then read two essays, one praising and one criticizing the United States, and rated their liking for each author.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
post: American students wrote about their own death or about watching television. Then they read two essays, one praising the United States and one criticizing it, and rated how much they liked each author. Students who wrote about their own death liked the author who praised the country more than the one who criticized it.

claim: Once the ratings began, the children's misbehavior dropped sharply compared with before.
post: Eight of the most disruptive children in a third grade class were watched to see how often they misbehaved. Then the teacher began giving them ratings that they could trade for candy and small trinkets. Once the ratings began, the children's misbehavior dropped sharply compared with before.

claim: All four learners learned the words faster with the check-each-word version.
post: Four learners were taught to read sets of four sight words. In one version, a set counted as learned only when the average across all four words was perfect. In the other, each word was checked on its own, and a new word replaced it as soon as it was learned. All four learners learned the words faster with the check-each-word version.

claim: Their views fell into two kinds of thinking: a selective one that treated intelligence as natural, and a comprehensive one that saw intelligence as depending on a person's social surroundings.
post: Finnish parents and teachers answered surveys about the school reforms going on at the time. Their views fell into two kinds of thinking: a selective one that treated intelligence as natural, and a comprehensive one that saw intelligence as depending on a person's social surroundings.

claim: Over time the entire population moved to the group with punishment, and the group without it emptied out.
post: People played a cooperation game and chose which of two groups to be in, one where members could punish others and one where they could not. Over time the entire population moved to the group with punishment, and the group without it emptied out.

claim: The therapy group showed a bigger increase in meaning in life than the waiting group, right after the sessions and a month later.
post: Female college students who were very concerned about their weight and body shape were randomly split into two groups. One group had six weekly one-on-one therapy sessions focused on finding meaning in life. The other group waited seven weeks without sessions. The therapy group showed a bigger increase in meaning in life than the waiting group, right after the sessions and a month later.

claim: The children made substantially fewer of these sounds than in the times before the teacher did this.
post: Children with autism who often made repetitive, purposeless sounds worked with a teacher. Whenever a child made those sounds, the teacher gave easy spoken requests until the child followed three in a row without them. The children made substantially fewer of these sounds than in the times before the teacher did this.

claim: Parents had a positive attitude toward aerobic exercise but a less positive one toward strength exercise.
post: Parents of kids aged 12 to 15 filled out an online survey about their child's exercise. They rated how they felt about their child doing aerobic exercise, which gets the heart pumping, and strength exercise, such as lifting weights. Parents had a positive attitude toward aerobic exercise but a less positive one toward strength exercise.

claim: All three birds eventually shifted as that rule predicted.
post: Pigeons pecked either of two keys to earn rewards. In one setup, the birds spent most of their time on the left key. In the other, a "stick with what pays best right now" rule predicted a move to the right key, even though that cut their rewards. All three birds eventually shifted as that rule predicted.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: Men and women differed a lot in which kind of unfaithfulness upset them more.
post: Men and women were each asked to imagine their partner being unfaithful in two ways: having sex with someone else, or becoming emotionally close to someone else. They picked which would upset them more. Men and women differed a lot in which kind of unfaithfulness upset them more.

claim: Looking at just the first 3 to 5 minutes, the cause was identified in 80% of the 30 cases.
post: After an interview about a person's problem behavior, practitioners ran test sessions that combined the likely triggers and rewards to see what kept the behavior going. A full test took about 25 minutes on average. Looking at just the first 3 to 5 minutes, the cause was identified in 80% of the 30 cases.

claim: Older adults took longer to correct, made more rigid corrections, and ended up less accurate than younger adults.
post: Younger and older adults used a computer mouse to reach for a target on a screen. In some trials the target jumped to a new spot mid-reach, so they had to change course. Older adults took longer to correct, made more rigid corrections, and ended up less accurate than younger adults.

claim: Adults remembered a new word better when it went against a stronger expectation than when it went against a weaker one.
post: Adults learned made-up names for objects, each one placed in a sentence. Some sentences strongly suggested what the thing would be, while others left it more open. Adults remembered a new word better when it went against a stronger expectation than when it went against a weaker one.

claim: People who wrote "Will I" solved more of the anagrams than people in any other group.
post: People were told they would be doing a handwriting task. They wrote either "Will I" or "I will" 20 times, plus two groups who wrote just "I" or just "Will." Then everyone tried to unscramble 10 words into new words. People who wrote "Will I" solved more of the anagrams than people in any other group.

claim: The more negatively a scenario was judged by others, the more shame people said they would feel.
post: People read 29 short scenarios, such as doing a bad job caring for your children or having poor table manners. Some rated how negatively they would view another person in each scenario. A different group rated how much shame they would feel if it were them. The more negatively a scenario was judged by others, the more shame people said they would feel.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: The scales rated the team tasks differently from the individual tasks.
post: College men trained for two weeks in four-person teams on a computer-simulated combat mission. Some tasks in it were done alone, and others needed the whole team. Each task was rated on new scales meant to show how team-based it is. The scales rated the team tasks differently from the individual tasks.
journal: Human Factors The Journal of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society

claim: On a test given later, the group that chose when to get feedback did better than the group that did not.
post: People practiced a timing task that involved pressing keys in a set sequence. One group could ask for feedback on how they did whenever they wanted it. A second group got feedback on a schedule they had no say in. On a test given later, the group that chose when to get feedback did better than the group that did not.
journal: Research Quarterly for Exercise and Sport

claim: Athletes who scored higher on hardiness and resilience reported the highest quality of life.
post: Adult wheelchair basketball players filled out questionnaires about how gritty, hardy and resilient they are, and how satisfied they are with their lives. Athletes who scored higher on hardiness and resilience reported the highest quality of life.

claim: Students who did the program improved on all three, while the waiting-list students did not change.
post: Students were randomly split into two groups. One group started a two-week mindfulness program on their own online right away, and the other group was put on a waiting list. Everyone answered questions about mindfulness, stress, and anxiety or low mood before and after. Students who did the program improved on all three, while the waiting-list students did not change.

claim: All 18 skills taught with the teaching interaction procedure were mastered, versus only 4 of 18 taught with social stories.
post: Boys with autism were taught social skills, like facing someone and looking them in the eye, in two different ways. Each boy learned some skills with one method and some with the other, in the same number of sessions. All 18 skills taught with the teaching interaction procedure were mastered, versus only 4 of 18 taught with social stories.

claim: People in the fast task with a witness were more likely to sign a confession than those in the slow task with no witness.
post: People did a reaction-time task at a fast or slow pace, then were falsely accused of hitting a wrong key that damaged the computer. Another person said she either saw them hit it or saw nothing. People in the fast task with a witness were more likely to sign a confession than those in the slow task with no witness.

claim: By third grade, children's ideas started to fit together, but younger children expected less of a link than older children or adults.
post: Children in grades 1 to 7 and adults thought about traits of people, some familiar and some new to them. They reasoned about ideas like a trait being there from birth and a trait never changing. By third grade, children's ideas started to fit together, but younger children expected less of a link than older children or adults.

claim: Speech tended to be picked up better with a happy face than with a sad or neutral one, on both sides of the face.
post: People watched and listened to a talker say sentences in a happy, sad, or neutral way. In some videos they could see only the left half or only the right half of the talker's face. Speech tended to be picked up better with a happy face than with a sad or neutral one, on both sides of the face.

claim: Among mothers who feared it little, the two were not related.
post: Mothers of children five and under filled out an online survey. It asked how much shame they felt, how far they fell short of the kind of mother they wanted to be, and how much they feared being judged by others. Among mothers who greatly feared being judged, falling short of their ideal went with much more shame. Among mothers who feared it little, the two were not related.
journal: Journal of Child and Family Studies

claim: Even 3-year-olds judged others' thoughts about pretend happenings accurately, and did less well on the wrong-belief task.
post: Three- and four-year-olds were asked what an absent puppet or person would think about a pretend game whose make-believe setup had been changed. The children also did a standard task about what someone else wrongly believes. Even 3-year-olds judged others' thoughts about pretend happenings accurately, and did less well on the wrong-belief task.

claim: Older patients and male patients were offered more help and seen as in more pain than younger and female patients.
post: Young and older adults pretended to be healthcare workers. They rated how much pain patients seemed to be in and offered them help. The patients were younger and older, men and women. Older patients and male patients were offered more help and seen as in more pain than younger and female patients.

claim: Women who went through the severe, embarrassing entry test rated the group as more attractive than the others did.
post: Women volunteered to join a group discussion about sex. Before joining, some read very embarrassing sexual material aloud, some read only mildly embarrassing words aloud, and some read nothing. Then everyone listened to the same recorded discussion and rated the group. Women who went through the severe, embarrassing entry test rated the group as more attractive than the others did.
journal: The Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology

claim: Using their own name gave a smaller brain signal of emotional reaction to upsetting pictures than using "I," with no rise in a signal of mental effort.
post: People viewed upsetting and neutral pictures while thinking about their feelings, with brain activity recorded. Sometimes they used "I" to think about it, other times their own name. Using their own name gave a smaller brain signal of emotional reaction to upsetting pictures than using "I," with no rise in a signal of mental effort.

claim: The rats that had gotten immediate rewards picked the larger, later reward less often than the comparison group.
post: Rats spent time getting rewards right away. A comparison group was only handled and left to grow up. Then all the rats chose between a smaller reward and a larger reward that came later. The rats that had gotten immediate rewards picked the larger, later reward less often than the comparison group.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: The answers fell into three distinct groups: low, medium and high sensitivity to surroundings.
post: Children and teenagers in the UK filled out a short 12-question survey about how much they are shaped by the world around them. Researchers then used a statistical method to sort the answers into groups of similar kids. The answers fell into three distinct groups: low, medium and high sensitivity to surroundings.

claim: Explorers mostly did better with little experience, while the familiar-approach students mostly did better with a lot.
post: Students tried two puzzles that need a creative trick to solve. Some liked exploring new approaches and others liked sticking with familiar ones, and they also differed in prior experience. Explorers mostly did better with little experience, while the familiar-approach students mostly did better with a lot.

claim: The cartoons ranked as more aggressive were also ranked as funnier.
post: Some people ranked sets of cartoons from magazines by how funny they were, and others ranked the same cartoons by how aggressive they were. The cartoons ranked as more aggressive were also ranked as funnier.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: For 7 of the 9 students, how they did in training was related to how they did on the skill checks.
post: Students with autism did a set of skill checks, including matching, imitating, scanning, and telling sounds apart and pictures apart. Later they trained to connect spoken sounds with pictures. For 7 of the 9 students, how they did in training was related to how they did on the skill checks.

claim: The 80% goal was sometimes not enough for skills to last.
post: People with developmental disabilities were taught new skills, and teaching stopped once they hit an accuracy goal. The goals differed, including the common one of 80% correct in three sessions in a row. Later, researchers checked whether the skills stuck. The 80% goal was sometimes not enough for skills to last.

claim: The 18-month-olds took the adult's belief into account when working out how to help him.
post: Toddlers got a chance to help an adult reach his goal. To work out what he wanted, they had to notice whether he wrongly believed a toy was inside a box. The 18-month-olds took the adult's belief into account when working out how to help him.

claim: Only the students in the listening training improved their communication skills, though all three groups grew more confident.
post: College psychology students spent a semester either learning listening skills in a 10-week training, staffing a helpline after passing that training, or working at a community agency. Everyone's communication was tested at the start and end. Only the students in the listening training improved their communication skills, though all three groups grew more confident.

claim: The share of teens who seemed to understand the question and could talk about their own meaning was just as high as in the older groups.
post: Young teens were asked about the meaning of life and what it meant in their own lives. Earlier studies had only asked college students and older adults. The share of teens who seemed to understand the question and could talk about their own meaning was just as high as in the older groups.

claim: Looking back at their answers, those people had become more anxious and emotionally unstable in the years before their diagnosis.
post: Adults aged 80 and older answered questions about their personality, such as whether they feel anxious or are extra sensitive, about every two years. Some were later diagnosed with dementia. Looking back at their answers, those people had become more anxious and emotionally unstable in the years before their diagnosis.
journal: The Journals of Gerontology Series B

claim: Parents of children with Down syndrome looked better off than the other parents, but after accounting for family income, that advantage disappeared.
post: Married couples with a young child with an intellectual disability filled out questionnaires about their mood and support, and were watched with their child. Some children had Down syndrome; others had a different disability. Parents of children with Down syndrome looked better off than the other parents, but after accounting for family income, that advantage disappeared.

claim: Almost half of all the reported lies came from just 5% of the people.
post: A national group of adults was asked to report how many lies they had told in the past 24 hours. Some people reported none, while a few reported many. Almost half of all the reported lies came from just 5% of the people.

claim: Counting each item on its own took fewer sessions of name training for 3 of the 5 people.
post: Five people with autism were taught new skills, like naming things, over many training sessions. In one version, each item was counted as learned on its own. In the other, a whole set of items had to be learned together. Counting each item on its own took fewer sessions of name training for 3 of the 5 people.

claim: The right one came out on top in 32% of sessions, versus 25% expected by chance.
post: One person described their thoughts aloud in a quiet room while another, in a separate room, focused on a randomly chosen picture or video clip. Afterward the first person rated four clips, one being that clip, for how well each matched their thoughts. The right one came out on top in 32% of sessions, versus 25% expected by chance.

claim: The older children showed more wholehearted helping and more flat-out refusing than the toddlers did.
post: Families with a mother, a father, a 16-month-old toddler, and an older brother or sister took part in a family cleanup session. Researchers watched how the children responded when their parents asked them to help. The older children showed more wholehearted helping and more flat-out refusing than the toddlers did.

claim: Those oddly spelled words were read 39 milliseconds faster when the second task was harder.
post: People read words out loud while doing a second task at the same time. The second task was harder for some and easier for others. Some of the words were spelled in ways that don't match how they sound. Those oddly spelled words were read 39 milliseconds faster when the second task was harder.

claim: Babies hearing one word twice looked longer at two different objects than two identical ones; babies hearing two words showed a different pattern.
post: Babies watched a box open to show two objects, identical or different. Later, before the box opened, a voice named the contents with one made-up word twice or two different made-up words. Babies hearing one word twice looked longer at two different objects than two identical ones; babies hearing two words showed a different pattern.

claim: Instead of the two groups many theories expect, people fell into three: low, medium and high sensitivity.
post: College students rated how much statements like "Are you easily overwhelmed by strong sensory input?" described them. Researchers had a computer sort them into groups by answer pattern, without choosing the groups in advance. Instead of the two groups many theories expect, people fell into three: low, medium and high sensitivity.

claim: Those who got the early guesses right rated themselves as better at predicting coin tosses than the other two groups did.
post: Men guessed heads or tails for a series of coin tosses. Some got many right early and fewer later, others did worse early and better later, and others had a random mix of hits and misses. Those who got the early guesses right rated themselves as better at predicting coin tosses than the other two groups did.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: People with lower self-esteem were more depressed later on, but being depressed did not predict lower self-esteem later.
post: Teens and young adults filled out questionnaires about their self-esteem and their depression, four times over several years. Researchers then checked which one came first. People with lower self-esteem were more depressed later on, but being depressed did not predict lower self-esteem later.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: People judged objects as smaller when their hand was magnified.
post: People judged how big objects were while their hands were magnified or not magnified. People judged objects as smaller when their hand was magnified.
journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

claim: The coaching group lost about 5.7 kg (6.1% of their starting weight) by month 6 and largely kept it off.
post: Women with obesity were randomly put into one of two weight-loss programs. One group got a printed manual and follow-up phone calls. The other group got exercise coaching, then two months later group sessions on using the same self-control skills to eat in a controlled way. The coaching group lost about 5.7 kg (6.1% of their starting weight) by month 6 and largely kept it off.

claim: By the end, children in the program classrooms were better at blending sounds into words and at knowing which sounds go with which letters than children in the other classrooms.
post: Teachers in kindergarten and first-grade classrooms across Canada used a web-based reading program with their classes for a full semester, about 20 hours per child. Other classrooms did not use it. By the end, children in the program classrooms were better at blending sounds into words and at knowing which sounds go with which letters than children in the other classrooms.

claim: Religious people were more affected by the religious music than non-religious people were.
post: People heard two minutes of religious music, regular music, or white noise through headphones. Then they did number puzzles and marked on a sheet how many they solved, with more money for more solved, so they could lie. Religious people were more affected by the religious music than non-religious people were.

claim: In both kinds of groups, people who started with the least positive attitudes improved greatly, while those who started with the most positive worsened greatly.
post: People filled out a survey on their attitudes toward stuttering, then filled it out again later. In between, some were given something meant to improve attitudes and others were not. In both kinds of groups, people who started with the least positive attitudes improved greatly, while those who started with the most positive worsened greatly.

claim: People were faster to decide with the turned letters than with the upright ones.
post: People saw strings of letters stacked in a column and decided whether each was a real word. In one version every letter stood upright. In the other every letter was turned on its side, as if the whole word had been rotated. People were faster to decide with the turned letters than with the upright ones.

claim: Attention followed the robot's gaze more strongly when it had first made eye contact than when it had avoided their eyes.
post: People sat facing a humanoid robot that looked off to one side. Sometimes it first looked right into the person's eyes before looking away, and sometimes it avoided their eyes. Attention followed the robot's gaze more strongly when it had first made eye contact than when it had avoided their eyes.

claim: Afterward, all three did this when approached again, and they still did it a month or so later.
post: Three boys with autism were each approached by an unfamiliar adult who tried to lure them away with lines like "Come with me" or "Come see the Xbox in my car." Then they were taught to say no, run to a safe place, and tell a grown-up. Afterward, all three did this when approached again, and they still did it a month or so later.

claim: Having just faced a clash made the next clash easier, and that benefit did not differ in size between weak and strong clashes, in reaction times or a brain signal.
post: People did a computer task where distracting items either agreed with the right answer, clashed with it a little, or clashed with it a lot. Stronger clashes made people slower. Having just faced a clash made the next clash easier, and that benefit did not differ in size between weak and strong clashes, in reaction times or a brain signal.

claim: People said they would show less pride when the achievement was relevant to the person watching.
post: People recalled or read about an achievement they were proud of and said how intensely they would show their pride to someone else. For some the achievement was relevant to that person, and for others it was not. People said they would show less pride when the achievement was relevant to the person watching.

claim: Fathers rated themselves higher than mothers rated themselves on math and spatial ability.
post: Parents were asked to rate how good they were at seven kinds of ability, including math, spatial skills, music, and getting along with people. Mothers and fathers each rated themselves. Fathers rated themselves higher than mothers rated themselves on math and spatial ability.

claim: A history of being teased was linked to how their body image and eating problems developed.
post: Teenage girls were measured on how heavy they were, how heavy they thought they were, and whether they had ever been teased about their weight or size. They also answered questions about their body image and eating. A history of being teased was linked to how their body image and eating problems developed.

claim: Children with one version of a brain-growth gene and two short copies of a serotonin gene had the highest depression scores, but only among the mistreated children.
post: Children gave a saliva sample for a DNA test and were assessed for signs of depression. Some had been mistreated and some had not. Children with one version of a brain-growth gene and two short copies of a serotonin gene had the highest depression scores, but only among the mistreated children.

claim: For two of the four students, the test agreed across both adults and the matched plan worked better.
post: Students who rarely finished schoolwork took a test of which reward would get them working, run by a researcher and by a teacher. Then they tried plans that matched the test result and plans that did not. For two of the four students, the test agreed across both adults and the matched plan worked better.

claim: Babies who saw the hand looked first at the same toy it had grabbed before, now in a new spot.
post: Babies watched short videos of a hand reaching for one of two toys, a frog or a ball. Then the toys switched places, and the hand stopped halfway between them. Other babies saw a plastic claw make the same moves. Babies who saw the hand looked first at the same toy it had grabbed before, now in a new spot.

claim: After the human-like robot they did so more than at the start; after the machine-like one, no change.
post: People spent a short time with a humanoid robot that acted either like a person or like a machine. Then researchers checked whether people explained the robot's actions by its thoughts and intentions, as we do for people. After the human-like robot they did so more than at the start; after the machine-like one, no change.

claim: The trained children's IQ scores rose after the first part and rose again after the second, compared with the no-training group.
post: Children did training sessions over several weeks that taught them how things relate, such as same, opposite, more than and less than. They took an IQ test before training, after the first part, and after the second part. A matched group got no training. The trained children's IQ scores rose after the first part and rose again after the second, compared with the no-training group.

claim: People who wrote to their future self were less inclined to make delinquent choices.
post: Some people wrote a letter to their future self and others did not. Then they made choices that could be delinquent. People who wrote to their future self were less inclined to make delinquent choices.

claim: Afterward, about 30% of people recalled at least one of those made-up details as part of their own memory.
post: People recalled four events from their own lives. A week later, each one described those events to another person, who was secretly working with the researchers, and heard that person's scripted "memories." The partner then slipped two new details into a summary of each person's story. Afterward, about 30% of people recalled at least one of those made-up details as part of their own memory.
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition

claim: Within a split second of seeing the picture, an early brain response was larger after hearing a word than after hearing the matching sound.
post: People heard either a spoken word, like "dog," or a matching sound, like a bark. A second later a picture appeared, and they pressed a button to say whether it matched what they heard. Their brain activity was recorded the whole time. Within a split second of seeing the picture, an early brain response was larger after hearing a word than after hearing the matching sound.

claim: European Canadians formed more explanations about personality than about the situation, while Japanese people formed both about equally.
post: European Canadians and Japanese people got information about someone's behavior that could be explained by the kind of person they are or by the situation they were in. Researchers measured which explanations people formed on their own. European Canadians formed more explanations about personality than about the situation, while Japanese people formed both about equally.

claim: Trained teachers gave better explicit instruction and gave students more, and more accurate, chances to practice together.
post: Sixteen schools were randomly split into two groups. In one group, first-grade teachers were trained to teach reading in a more explicit, step-by-step way, with ongoing coaching. Teachers in the other group did not get the training. Trained teachers gave better explicit instruction and gave students more, and more accurate, chances to practice together.

claim: Therapists put more of the cause on the client or outside circumstances when the client was their own.
post: Therapists read a short description of a client who quit therapy early. Some were told it was their own client, others that it was another therapist's client. Then they rated how likely each of several reasons was to have caused the client to quit. Therapists put more of the cause on the client or outside circumstances when the client was their own.

claim: Wives who started the relationship on birth control and later stopped were less satisfied if their husband's face was rated less attractive, but more satisfied if it was rated more attractive.
post: Newlywed wives reported their marital satisfaction over time and whether they used hormonal birth control. Trained raters scored each husband's face from a photo. Wives who started the relationship on birth control and later stopped were less satisfied if their husband's face was rated less attractive, but more satisfied if it was rated more attractive.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: Boldness was generally unrelated to these outcomes, and it rarely added anything beyond meanness and lack of restraint.
post: College students filled out a questionnaire that scored three sides of personality: boldness (staying calm and confident), meanness, and acting without restraint. Their scores were then compared with helpful and harmful outcomes. Boldness was generally unrelated to these outcomes, and it rarely added anything beyond meanness and lack of restraint.
journal: Personality Disorders: Theory, Research, and Treatment

claim: The questionnaire matched the interview with high accuracy, picking out most teens who had the diagnosis and most who didn't.
post: Teenagers staying in a psychiatric hospital filled out a questionnaire meant to spot borderline personality disorder. Trained staff also interviewed each teen to see who had the diagnosis. The questionnaire matched the interview with high accuracy, picking out most teens who had the diagnosis and most who didn't.

claim: How people were led to interpret it changed how much their expectations shifted afterward.
post: People who reported feeling quite depressed got feedback that went against what they had expected. The groups were led to interpret that feedback in different ways, such as explaining away evidence that contradicts what you believe. How people were led to interpret it changed how much their expectations shifted afterward.

claim: The babies tended to follow her gaze to the toy after the attention-grabbing moves, but not after she did nothing.
post: Babies watched videos of a woman looking down at a table with two toys. Before she turned to look at one toy, she did something different in each video: looked right at the baby, shivered, or did nothing. The babies tended to follow her gaze to the toy after the attention-grabbing moves, but not after she did nothing.

claim: The men on the scary bridge wrote stories with more sexual content and were more likely to try to contact her afterward.
post: Men crossing a scary suspension bridge or a non-scary bridge were approached by an attractive woman interviewer. She asked them to fill out a questionnaire that included writing stories about pictures. The men on the scary bridge wrote stories with more sexual content and were more likely to try to contact her afterward.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Within each day, people got faster with every repeat.
post: People looked at the same hidden-image picture, made of dots, five times a day for four days. Each time, researchers timed how long it took before the 3D shape popped out. Within each day, people got faster with every repeat.

claim: Babies expected two people who spoke the same language to be more likely to get along than two who spoke different languages.
post: Babies watched two people each tell a short story, both in English for some babies, and one in English and one in Spanish for others. Then the two either waved and smiled at each other or turned away with arms crossed. Babies expected two people who spoke the same language to be more likely to get along than two who spoke different languages.

claim: They used a considerably greater variety of strategies for building meaning from the story than for checking or fixing their understanding.
post: Deaf elementary school students read a short story one page at a time. After each page, they said out loud, or signed, what they were thinking as they read. They used a considerably greater variety of strategies for building meaning from the story than for checking or fixing their understanding.
journal: Journal of Deaf Studies and Deaf Education

claim: For most of them, the setting changed how much they valued the money they would have to wait for.
post: People who gamble regularly and heavily chose between hypothetical money now and a larger amount later. Each person did this twice, once inside the betting facility where they usually gamble and once in a place like a coffee shop. For most of them, the setting changed how much they valued the money they would have to wait for.

claim: Compared with when he was not tracking, he spent more time on task, did less off-task behavior, and felt better about schoolwork.
post: A boy in a remedial class at an English secondary school kept track of his own study behavior. The self-tracking was used, then taken away, to see what changed. Compared with when he was not tracking, he spent more time on task, did less off-task behavior, and felt better about schoolwork.

claim: Every chimpanzee failed to plan ahead in the trading task, but three did plan in the tool task.
post: Chimpanzees were given two kinds of problems where they had to act now to get a reward later. One was a trading task. The other was a task where they had to use a tool. Every chimpanzee failed to plan ahead in the trading task, but three did plan in the tool task.

claim: Using only those scores, they correctly sorted 94% of the babies as securely or anxiously attached to their mothers.
post: Mothers and their 12-month-old babies were filmed in a room with no toys, while each mother filled out a questionnaire and the baby explored. Researchers scored how well each mother responded to her baby's cues. Using only those scores, they correctly sorted 94% of the babies as securely or anxiously attached to their mothers.

claim: By year's end, girls with more math-anxious teachers did worse at math than girls with less anxious teachers.
post: Female first- and second-grade teachers rated how anxious math situations make them feel, such as studying for a math test. Their students were tested in math at the start and end of the school year. By year's end, girls with more math-anxious teachers did worse at math than girls with less anxious teachers.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: People with more depression at the start had more anxiety later, and people with more anxiety at the start had more depression later, with replaying thoughts fully explaining both.
post: Adults reported their depression and anxiety symptoms, and how much they replay sad thoughts and problems in their heads. Their symptoms were measured again later. People with more depression at the start had more anxiety later, and people with more anxiety at the start had more depression later, with replaying thoughts fully explaining both.

claim: Owners with more hyperactive and impulsive symptoms scored higher on that focus.
post: Business owners in the United States and Spain were assessed for ADHD symptoms, such as being impulsive and hyperactive. They were also scored on how much their firms focus on innovation, acting early, and taking risks. Owners with more hyperactive and impulsive symptoms scored higher on that focus.

claim: People who were more anxious in general and who disliked uncertainty more each tended to worry more.
post: First-year psychology students filled out questionnaires about how anxious and tense they usually are, how much they dislike not knowing what will happen, and how much they worry. Researchers then compared the scores across the questionnaires. People who were more anxious in general and who disliked uncertainty more each tended to worry more.

claim: Singles who were more anxious and moody (higher neuroticism) were more likely to start one, and their neuroticism dropped once they were in a relationship.
post: Young adults in Germany were assessed on their personality and relationships three times over eight years. Some started their first partner relationship along the way, while others stayed single. Singles who were more anxious and moody (higher neuroticism) were more likely to start one, and their neuroticism dropped once they were in a relationship.

claim: Five reasons came up: wanting to learn and grow, enjoying working with others, feeling a duty to give back, wanting better teaching and patient care, and plain fun.
post: Doctors and scientists at one medical school who occasionally led workshops for other faculty were interviewed about why they do it. The talks were recorded and typed up, and the researchers sorted what people said into themes. Five reasons came up: wanting to learn and grow, enjoying working with others, feeling a duty to give back, wanting better teaching and patient care, and plain fun.

claim: People reminded of death blamed the severely injured victims more than people who were not reminded.
post: Some people were reminded of their own death and others were not. Then everyone read about injured people, some badly hurt and some only mildly, and rated how much each victim was to blame. People reminded of death blamed the severely injured victims more than people who were not reminded.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: About half the differences in gambling problems were due to genes, and there was no sign that growing up in the same home mattered.
post: Adult twins, some identical and some fraternal, answered a phone interview about their gambling and any problems it had caused. Researchers compared how alike the twins in each pair were, for identical versus fraternal twins. About half the differences in gambling problems were due to genes, and there was no sign that growing up in the same home mattered.

claim: Across studies, dyslexic readers had less of it in the same six areas, including the cerebellum and regions toward the back and sides of the brain.
post: Brain scan results from nine earlier studies were pooled, each comparing people with dyslexia to people without it. Grey matter, the tissue holding nerve cells, was the focus. Across studies, dyslexic readers had less of it in the same six areas, including the cerebellum and regions toward the back and sides of the brain.

claim: The older adults rated songs from their youth as the most emotional, and they remembered more about those songs too.
post: Older and younger adults listened to 20-second clips of popular songs from across the 20th century. They rated how emotional each song felt, and tried to name its title, artist, and year. The older adults rated songs from their youth as the most emotional, and they remembered more about those songs too.

claim: Same-sex pairs were rated as looking more alike than opposite-sex pairs.
post: People looked at pairs of adult faces and rated how similar the two faces looked. Some pairs were two people of the same sex, and others were one man and one woman. Same-sex pairs were rated as looking more alike than opposite-sex pairs.

claim: When tested, all four adults used the new responses with the other items from the matching set, as if each set were one group.
post: Adults learned that one response earned a reward with items from one set, and another with items from a second set. Then they learned a new response for just one item in each set. When tested, all four adults used the new responses with the other items from the matching set, as if each set were one group.

claim: People shown the options one at a time were less satisfied and less committed.
post: People chose from a set of options that were shown either one at a time or all at once. Then they rated how satisfied they were with their choice and how committed they felt to it. People shown the options one at a time were less satisfied and less committed.

claim: People with more of these problems reported worse marriages, even when their personality was taken into account.
post: Married couples were interviewed about rule-breaking as teens, antisocial behavior as adults, and heavy drinking. They also filled out a personality questionnaire and a survey on how well their marriage was going. People with more of these problems reported worse marriages, even when their personality was taken into account.

claim: Inkblot scores for things like stress tolerance and social adjustment were linked to passing, while the ability tests and personality scores were only weakly linked.
post: Men applying to the Norwegian Naval Special Forces took ability tests, a personality questionnaire, and the Rorschach test, where people say what they see in inkblots. Then everyone's pass or fail result in training was recorded. Inkblot scores for things like stress tolerance and social adjustment were linked to passing, while the ability tests and personality scores were only weakly linked.

claim: Unhelpful beliefs explained 36% of the differences in how lonely students felt, and helpful beliefs explained 23%.
post: University students from several countries filled out questionnaires about their beliefs and how lonely they felt. Some beliefs were unhelpful, like expecting the worst, and others were helpful, like accepting yourself. Unhelpful beliefs explained 36% of the differences in how lonely students felt, and helpful beliefs explained 23%.

claim: Teens whose parent reported less conflict than the teen did were rated as more hopeless.
post: Teenagers with depression and one of their parents each filled out a questionnaire, separately, about how much the two of them clash. A clinician who interviewed both then rated how hopeless the teen seemed. Teens whose parent reported less conflict than the teen did were rated as more hopeless.

claim: Students who were more mindful rated their health better and reported better sleep, more exercise and less binge eating, partly because they were less stressed.
post: College students filled out questionnaires about how mindful they were, how stressed they felt, how healthy they thought they were, and how they ate, slept and exercised. Nobody was split into groups. Students who were more mindful rated their health better and reported better sleep, more exercise and less binge eating, partly because they were less stressed.

claim: Those punished this way were more likely to have been violent than those who weren't, even after accounting for severe child abuse.
post: Young adults recalled how often parents slapped, spanked, or hit them with an object as kids. They said whether they had hit, shoved, or thrown something at a dating partner in the past year. Those punished this way were more likely to have been violent than those who weren't, even after accounting for severe child abuse.

claim: The children rated their attitudes toward communicating and their ability to make friends higher than before camp.
post: Children who stutter spent a week at an intensive therapy camp focused on their feelings and thoughts about stuttering. About a month later, they and their parents filled out questionnaires about talking, friendships and daily life. The children rated their attitudes toward communicating and their ability to make friends higher than before camp.

claim: People who rated themselves higher on motivation, empathy and planning also rated themselves as more grateful and more satisfied with life.
post: Adults from the community filled out four questionnaires about themselves. They rated how well they plan, stay motivated and understand others, and also how grateful, forgiving and satisfied with life they felt. People who rated themselves higher on motivation, empathy and planning also rated themselves as more grateful and more satisfied with life.

claim: Those who felt more uncomfortable improved more, and were likelier to recover, with the thinking therapy than the relationship one.
post: People with depression were randomly given one of two talk therapies: one about relationships, one about changing unhelpful thinking. Beforehand, they rated how uncomfortable they felt getting close to others. Those who felt more uncomfortable improved more, and were likelier to recover, with the thinking therapy than the relationship one.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: Teens with more borderline personality traits were more likely to over-read what the characters were thinking and feeling, giving explanations that went too far.
post: Teens staying at a psychiatric hospital watched a 15-minute film about four people at a dinner party. The film stopped many times to ask what a character was feeling or thinking. Teens with more borderline personality traits were more likely to over-read what the characters were thinking and feeling, giving explanations that went too far.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry

claim: The three people each showed a different pattern of preferences among the sight, sound, and touch events.
post: Three people with severe disabilities each used a switch they could press. A computer turned each press into something to see, hear, or feel, and recorded the presses. The three people each showed a different pattern of preferences among the sight, sound, and touch events.

claim: They rated the gay teacher as less credible than the straight teacher.
post: A man gave the same lecture on cultural influences to eight college classes, keeping his delivery natural and the same each time. What changed was his sexual orientation: gay in some classes, straight in others. Students then rated how credible he was as a teacher. They rated the gay teacher as less credible than the straight teacher.

claim: Native German speakers got a head start from both; Russian speakers who learned German got one only from the built kind.
post: People decided whether a string of letters made a real German word, right after a related word flashed too quickly to notice. The flashed word was either a new word built from the target or a grammar-ending form of it. Native German speakers got a head start from both; Russian speakers who learned German got one only from the built kind.

claim: Those who got less sound pressed more, and those who got more sound pressed less.
post: People could press a button to see a visual signal, and each press was followed by a sound. For some, pressing at their usual rate gave them less sound than they would normally choose to hear. For others, it gave them more sound than they would choose. Those who got less sound pressed more, and those who got more sound pressed less.

claim: Larger wards had more self-rejection, a good atmosphere went with less, and individualized treatment went with less only if it didn't hurt the atmosphere.
post: People in psychiatric hospital wards reported how much they rejected themselves. Wards differed in how individualized treatment was, how good the group atmosphere was, and how large they were. Larger wards had more self-rejection, a good atmosphere went with less, and individualized treatment went with less only if it didn't hurt the atmosphere.

claim: Women scored lower than men on the plain math test, but did not differ from men in the other two.
post: Men and women tried hard math problems. Some heard it was a math test, others a problem-solving task. A third group heard it was a math test, plus that stereotypes about women and math can hurt scores. Women scored lower than men on the plain math test, but did not differ from men in the other two.

claim: People who were more right about spoken clues were better at spotting truthful statements than people who were less right.
post: Police officers and college students said what clues they think give away a liar, and rated 17 things a person might say. Then they watched eight video clips and judged whether each person was telling the truth. People who were more right about spoken clues were better at spotting truthful statements than people who were less right.

claim: Good events softened the hit that bad events had on their self-esteem and gloomy thinking.
post: Twice a week for up to 10 weeks, people wrote down the good and bad things that happened to them that day. They also rated their self-esteem and how much they were thinking in gloomy, self-critical ways. On days with bad events, people felt worse about themselves when no good events happened. Good events softened the hit that bad events had on their self-esteem and gloomy thinking.

claim: Spotting the word was affected both by competition from other words the sounds could fit and by the speech's rhythm pattern.
post: People listened to strings of nonsense sounds and tried to spot a real word hidden inside. In some strings, the hidden word was also the start of a longer word. Spotting the word was affected both by competition from other words the sounds could fit and by the speech's rhythm pattern.
journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition

claim: On a later test, people had learned less from the answers they were told they got wrong than from the ones they were told they got right.
post: People answered two-choice questions and were then told whether they got each one right or wrong. Because there were only two options, either message revealed the correct answer. On a later test, people had learned less from the answers they were told they got wrong than from the ones they were told they got right.

claim: With either kind of hint, people came up with more ideas than with no hint.
post: People lay in a brain scanner and came up with design ideas for a problem. They tried it with a hint close to the problem, with a hint far from the problem, and with no hint at all. With either kind of hint, people came up with more ideas than with no hint.

claim: For the last few hours, people drew on memories of specific moments, but for the last few months they drew on general beliefs about what they are like.
post: People reported on their own emotions, either over the last few hours or over the last few months. The researchers tested what people draw on to answer. For the last few hours, people drew on memories of specific moments, but for the last few months they drew on general beliefs about what they are like.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: The anxiety program lowered people's fear of anxious feelings, and that in turn went with fewer insomnia symptoms a month later than the health information.
post: People did a short computer program in one of two versions. One version taught them about anxiety and had them practice bodily sensations that can feel scary. The other gave general health information. The anxiety program lowered people's fear of anxious feelings, and that in turn went with fewer insomnia symptoms a month later than the health information.

claim: After the election, Clinton supporters, whose candidate lost, reported more feelings of rejection and a lower mood than Trump supporters did.
post: Voters filled out a survey about how rejected and low they felt, once before and once after the 2016 presidential election. Some backed Donald Trump and some backed Hillary Clinton. After the election, Clinton supporters, whose candidate lost, reported more feelings of rejection and a lower mood than Trump supporters did.

claim: Students tended to read each passage the way their own background suggested, and their answers and recall matched that reading.
post: Physical education students and music education students each read two passages that could be understood in two different ways. One could be a prison break or a wrestling match, the other a card game or a woodwind rehearsal. Students tended to read each passage the way their own background suggested, and their answers and recall matched that reading.

claim: When the people in the photos were unattractive, men who were more attractive themselves gave higher attractiveness ratings than less attractive men did.
post: People looked at photographs of other people and rated how physically attractive each one was. The judges were photographed too, and their own looks were rated. When the people in the photos were unattractive, men who were more attractive themselves gave higher attractiveness ratings than less attractive men did.

claim: Those who also had panic disorder were more likely to report nightmares (96%) and insomnia (100%) than the other groups.
post: People who had been diagnosed with PTSD answered a large national health interview. Researchers sorted them by which other condition they also had: panic disorder, depression, generalized anxiety, or alcohol dependence. Those who also had panic disorder were more likely to report nightmares (96%) and insomnia (100%) than the other groups.

claim: Rats held the lever longer when the rule was on and shorter when it was removed, with both timings.
post: Rats pressed a lever to earn rewards. Sometimes they had to hold the lever down for a minimum time to get one, and later that rule was removed. Rewards came right away or 8 seconds late. Rats held the lever longer when the rule was on and shorter when it was removed, with both timings.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: People with OCD used all but distraction more often, while people without anxiety used distraction more.
post: People with OCD and people without anxiety problems were compared on how they handle unwanted, upsetting thoughts. The ways included distracting yourself, punishing yourself, rethinking the thought, turning to other people, and worrying. People with OCD used all but distraction more often, while people without anxiety used distraction more.

claim: Students in the classrooms that used the program spent more time on task than they had before it started.
post: Teachers in some elementary classrooms taught their students to get the teacher's attention politely, follow directions, and ignore classmates who misbehave. Teams of students then earned rewards for doing these things. Other teachers carried on as usual. Students in the classrooms that used the program spent more time on task than they had before it started.

claim: Mindfulness training raised the ability to watch feelings without reacting more than therapy did, and that helped explain broader awareness and, later, better skill at seeing bad situations differently.
post: People with social anxiety took a 12-week group course, either mindfulness training or cognitive-behavioral therapy. Questionnaires over the following year tracked their attention, awareness and mood. Mindfulness training raised the ability to watch feelings without reacting more than therapy did, and that helped explain broader awareness and, later, better skill at seeing bad situations differently.

claim: Before training they rated Black faces more negatively, but afterward the gap was no longer clear.
post: Children practiced a matching task that taught them to pair faces of Black people with a positive symbol. Before and after, they rated how they felt about Black and White faces. Before training they rated Black faces more negatively, but afterward the gap was no longer clear.

claim: When people had the choice, they reported feeling less negative than when the same pictures were imposed.
post: People looked at upsetting pictures, like spiders, snakes or mistreated animals. Sometimes they chose between two labeled kinds of picture before seeing one. Other times the same pictures were simply shown to them. When people had the choice, they reported feeling less negative than when the same pictures were imposed.

claim: Most of the words people listed were about sensory qualities, like "warm" or "see-through," and most of those were about touch.
post: Students had a limited amount of time to write down adjectives that describe how materials look and feel, such as leather, metal, and wood. Most of the words people listed were about sensory qualities, like "warm" or "see-through," and most of those were about touch.
journal: Psychology of Aesthetics Creativity and the Arts

claim: People who had eaten the sweet food rated themselves as more agreeable and helped more.
post: Some people ate a sweet food, some a food that was not sweet, and some no food. Then they rated how agreeable they were. People who had eaten the sweet food rated themselves as more agreeable and helped more.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: All the groups improved by about the same amount, so the different therapies had roughly equal results.
post: Patients at 58 NHS clinics in the UK got one of three kinds of talk therapy: cognitive-behavioral, person-centered or psychodynamic. Some also got one extra approach added. Everyone filled out the same symptom questionnaire at the start and end of treatment. All the groups improved by about the same amount, so the different therapies had roughly equal results.

claim: The more social anxiety symptoms people had, the more they tended to overestimate how bad they and the other person would feel.
post: Young adults read short made-up scenes in which they made another person feel angry, disgusted, or happy. They then predicted how strongly they and the other person would feel. The more social anxiety symptoms people had, the more they tended to overestimate how bad they and the other person would feel.

claim: Women whose eating style was intuitive, meaning they eat by hunger and fullness, were more satisfied with their bodies than the other women.
post: Mothers whose youngest child was between 6 months and 4 years old filled out an online survey. It asked about how they eat, how they feel about their bodies, their attitudes toward food, and their mood. Women whose eating style was intuitive, meaning they eat by hunger and fullness, were more satisfied with their bodies than the other women.
journal: Journal of Reproductive and Infant Psychology

claim: People who got oxytocin made these judgments faster than people who got the plain spray.
post: Men got a nasal spray with either oxytocin, a hormone linked to social bonding, or a spray with no active ingredient. Then, in a brain scanner, they judged whether trait words like "clever" or "lazy" described themselves, their mother, a classmate, or a stranger. People who got oxytocin made these judgments faster than people who got the plain spray.

claim: Pictures of food made hungry people worse at spotting the target.
post: People watched a rapid stream of images and tried to spot a target that came right after an irrelevant picture. They did this when hungry and when full. Pictures of food made hungry people worse at spotting the target.

claim: People who agreed with this kind of reasoning more had more OCD symptoms, even when general distress and OCD-related beliefs were taken into account.
post: People online did a new reasoning task, then answered questions about their OCD symptoms. The task measured inverse reasoning, which means drawing conclusions about reality from imagined causes. People who agreed with this kind of reasoning more had more OCD symptoms, even when general distress and OCD-related beliefs were taken into account.

claim: Those people were more likely to stop binge eating and improved more in eating problems and mood than people who didn't.
post: Overweight people with binge eating disorder did a guided self-help program, either one about changing eating habits or one about losing weight. Some cut their binge eating by about two-thirds within four weeks. Those people were more likely to stop binge eating and improved more in eating problems and mood than people who didn't.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: A foreign language led to less negative feelings about bad-luck scenarios and less positive feelings about good-luck scenarios.
post: People read scenarios in their native language or in a foreign language. In each, they imagined doing something under a superstitious circumstance, such as a broken mirror or a four-leaf clover, and rated how they would feel. A foreign language led to less negative feelings about bad-luck scenarios and less positive feelings about good-luck scenarios.

claim: In both groups, all 11 sets of questions sorted into two kinds of motivation: reasons coming from inside the person and reasons coming from outside.
post: Environmental activists in the US Midwest, and others tied to climate summits in Peru and Paris, answered questions about why they do their activism, drawn from two different theories. In both groups, all 11 sets of questions sorted into two kinds of motivation: reasons coming from inside the person and reasons coming from outside.

claim: Over half of them lacked specific knowledge of basic fertility principles.
post: Transgender and gender expansive teens and young adults at a university clinic answered a 22-question survey about fertility and about whether they might want to be parents someday. There was no comparison group. Over half of them lacked specific knowledge of basic fertility principles.

claim: Some of it remained beyond that.
post: People filled out an online survey. It asked how much they enjoy thinking, whether they get started on tasks at once or think about other things first, and how well they resist temptation. People who enjoy thinking reported more self-control, and part of that link ran through getting started at once. Some of it remained beyond that.

claim: How the tokens were split between the sets differed markedly depending on whether YIM was called good or bad.
post: People learned to group nonsense words into two sets of three. Then they were told one word, YIM, was a good person, and later that it was a bad person. Each time, they placed tokens on the words however they liked. How the tokens were split between the sets differed markedly depending on whether YIM was called good or bad.

claim: The results differed little between the two kinds of countries.
post: People in 36 countries did a set of well-known psychology tasks on a computer, some in a lab and some online, with the order of tasks varied. Researchers then compared results from rich, Western-style countries with results from less Western, less rich ones. The results differed little between the two kinds of countries.
journal: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science

claim: Readers' eye movements showed they kept some doubt about words already read, and revised it based on later words.
post: People read sentences while a camera tracked their eyes. Some sentences had an early word with look-alike words of a different grammar type, and a later word that fit those look-alikes well or poorly. Readers' eye movements showed they kept some doubt about words already read, and revised it based on later words.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: Afterward, women who saw attractive models reported stronger intentions, attitudes, and social pressure to lose weight than women who saw unattractive models.
post: Women browsed a fashion website that showed pictures of models. Some saw attractive models and others saw unattractive ones, and the models were either thin or obese. Afterward, women who saw attractive models reported stronger intentions, attitudes, and social pressure to lose weight than women who saw unattractive models.

claim: People who were willing to donate reported more lifetime, casual, and past-year sex partners than people who were not.
post: People played a money game where they could keep their possible winnings or donate them. They also reported how many sex partners they had had. People who were willing to donate reported more lifetime, casual, and past-year sex partners than people who were not.

claim: The way a gamble was described shifted people's choices more when they had to decide fast.
post: People chose between gambles described in terms of gains or in terms of losses. Some choices had to be made under time pressure and others not. The way a gamble was described shifted people's choices more when they had to decide fast.

claim: Children with more severe stuttering needed longer treatment than children with less severe stuttering.
post: Preschool children who stuttered went through a treatment program called the Lidcombe Program, and clinicians tracked how many clinic visits each child needed before the stuttering was zero or nearly gone. Researchers then compared children who stuttered more severely at the start with those who stuttered less. Children with more severe stuttering needed longer treatment than children with less severe stuttering.
journal: Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research

claim: Women who were very concerned about their bodies felt better about their bodies and themselves after seeing their own body paired with smiles.
post: Women watched pictures of their own bodies flash on a screen, each followed by a face. For some, their own body was paired with a smiling face. For others, the faces were random.
