Women who were very concerned about their bodies felt better about their bodies and themselves after seeing their own body paired with smiles.

claim: Lying took longer than telling the truth in both languages, but the gap in answer time was smaller in English than in German.
post: German speakers answered questions, some in German and some in English. A color cue told them on each question whether to answer truthfully or lie. Lying took longer than telling the truth in both languages, but the gap in answer time was smaller in English than in German.

claim: In both age groups, Americans were more likely than Chinese to answer as if a name sticks to the person first given it.
post: Children and adults in the U.S. and China heard a story based on a famous puzzle about names, where a famous deed turns out to belong to someone else. They then judged statements using the name. In both age groups, Americans were more likely than Chinese to answer as if a name sticks to the person first given it.

claim: A month later, all three could pick out the objects on their own.
post: Three preschoolers with very little speech were taught the names of everyday objects by a speech therapist. They practiced matching each object to an identical picture, and the therapist gave physical prompts to help. A month later, all three could pick out the objects on their own.

claim: The students who were more grateful reported better psychological well-being and more satisfaction with life.
post: College students filled out questionnaires about how grateful they are, how well they feel they are doing psychologically, and how satisfied they are with their lives. Nobody was split into groups. The students who were more grateful reported better psychological well-being and more satisfaction with life.

claim: People identified brand names faster in their usual case.
post: People decided whether a word was a brand name. Brand names were shown in their usual case, such as adidas and IKEA, or in the other case, such as ADIDAS and ikea. People identified brand names faster in their usual case.

claim: In both the children's and the parents' ratings, the answers grouped into three related kinds of sensitivity to unfairness.
post: Children, their parents, or both rated how each child notices and reacts badly to unfairness. The ratings asked about being treated unfairly, watching others be treated unfairly, and being the one who acts unfairly. In both the children's and the parents' ratings, the answers grouped into three related kinds of sensitivity to unfairness.

claim: Income rank predicted life satisfaction, while the amount earned and the comparison with the typical income did not.
post: People reported their income and how satisfied they were with their life. Researchers then checked three things: how much money each person made, where that income ranked within a comparison group, and how it compared with the group's typical income. Income rank predicted life satisfaction, while the amount earned and the comparison with the typical income did not.

claim: That link was stronger in women who watch their looks closely, worry a lot, or have a family member and a friend with an eating disorder than in other women.
post: College women answered questions about their eating habits, their body image, and their personality. Women unhappier with their bodies reported more eating disorder symptoms. That link was stronger in women who watch their looks closely, worry a lot, or have a family member and a friend with an eating disorder than in other women.

claim: Learners overwhelmingly favored the meaning-based order over the English-like one.
post: People learned a made-up language from English phrases like "purple vase" heard as "vase purple." No phrase had two describing words. At test, they picked between an order that kept English-like word order and one that followed the structure of the meaning. Learners overwhelmingly favored the meaning-based order over the English-like one.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: When they were simply placed in sequence, people's overall rating ended up similar to their answer on the specific question.
post: People answered a question about one part of their life, then rated how satisfied they were with their life overall. In one version, the two questions were just placed one after the other with no link between them. When they were simply placed in sequence, people's overall rating ended up similar to their answer on the specific question.

claim: Of everything asked, the number of violent acts a person had committed best predicted how much they found violence enjoyable.
post: Former fighters in eastern Congo gave long one-on-one interviews at a camp for people leaving armed groups. They were asked about violence they had seen, suffered and committed, and whether fighting felt thrilling. Of everything asked, the number of violent acts a person had committed best predicted how much they found violence enjoyable.

claim: The gene version was linked to quitting, not to starting: people who carried it were more likely to have quit.
post: Adults who had never smoked, who currently smoked, or who used to smoke were checked for one particular version of a gene tied to the brain's dopamine system. They also had their personality measured. The gene version was linked to quitting, not to starting: people who carried it were more likely to have quit.

claim: Among women in long-term relationships, those with higher average progesterone over the cycle chose masculine faces less often.
post: Women gave a saliva sample every morning for one menstrual cycle. At three visits during the cycle, they looked at pairs of men's faces and picked one from each pair. The faces in a pair differed only in how masculine they looked. Among women in long-term relationships, those with higher average progesterone over the cycle chose masculine faces less often.

claim: The more times a meaning appeared, the more accurately people recalled it.
post: People read a long story online that gave familiar words, like "foam," a new made-up meaning, such as a safe hidden inside a piece of furniture. Each new meaning showed up two, four, six, or eight times in the story. Later, people were asked to recall the meanings. The more times a meaning appeared, the more accurately people recalled it.

claim: Students who had played the game rated fake news articles as less reliable and less persuasive.
post: High school students either played a game in which they made a misleading news article about a politicized issue, or did not. Then they rated how reliable and persuasive fake news articles were. Students who had played the game rated fake news articles as less reliable and less persuasive.

claim: They did well with new shapes they already had steady labels for, and poorly with new shapes they didn't.
post: Children had to pick the shape turned a quarter turn clockwise from a shape they were shown. They were taught to label which way the first shape pointed, adjust the label for the turn, and repeat it at the choices. They did well with new shapes they already had steady labels for, and poorly with new shapes they didn't.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: Destinations they had picked were rated higher afterward than before.
post: People rated how happy they would be on 80 vacation destinations. Then they were told they would pick between two destinations flashed too fast to see, but only scribbles were shown. After each pick, the names were revealed. Destinations they had picked were rated higher afterward than before.

claim: Those who saw mostly the suspect judged the confession as less forced than those who saw both equally, and those who saw mostly the detective judged it as the most forced.
post: College students watched a video of a mock police interrogation that ended in a confession. For some the camera mostly showed the suspect, for others mostly the detective, and for others both equally. Those who saw mostly the suspect judged the confession as less forced than those who saw both equally, and those who saw mostly the detective judged it as the most forced.

claim: Quiz scores improved in every group, and were higher overall when the extra credit depended on the group.
post: Future teachers in a college course took weekly quizzes. In one condition, a group earned extra credit points if the group scored 80% or higher. In the other, each person earned extra credit by scoring 80% or higher on their own. Quiz scores improved in every group, and were higher overall when the extra credit depended on the group.

claim: They preferred the ones matching the teacher, not the earlier student.
post: People heard made-up words from two voices, a "teacher" and a "student." One voice began each word with a short delay on the first sound, the other with a long delay, and for other people the two were swapped. Later they judged a new student's pronunciations. They preferred the ones matching the teacher, not the earlier student.

claim: The more devastated people's own area was, the less concern they showed.
post: A few weeks after a huge earthquake in China, adults filled out a questionnaire. Some lived far from the damage and others lived in badly hit areas. They estimated things like the chance of an epidemic and how many doctors and safety measures were needed. The more devastated people's own area was, the less concern they showed.

claim: The estimates differed from test to test: the NART gave the highest estimate and the TOPF the lowest.
post: Adults, none of them with any known impairment, took several reading tests that are used to estimate what a person's IQ was before an illness or injury. Each test turned the person's score into an estimate of their IQ. The estimates differed from test to test: the NART gave the highest estimate and the TOPF the lowest.

claim: Teenagers aged 14 to 17 made more errors than adults.
post: People from age 7 to adulthood saw a set of shelves with objects and moved objects as a director instructed. The director could see only some of the objects, so people had to move only the ones the director could see. Teenagers aged 14 to 17 made more errors than adults.

claim: Soldiers who had been worse at unlearning that fear had more severe posttraumatic stress symptoms later.
post: Before a four-month deployment to Afghanistan, Dutch soldiers did a learning task that measured how well they could stop fearing a signal that no longer meant danger. After coming home, they reported their stress symptoms. Soldiers who had been worse at unlearning that fear had more severe posttraumatic stress symptoms later.

claim: Students who enjoyed hard thinking more also scored better on almost all of these.
post: Students training to become teachers were measured on how much they enjoy hard mental work. They were also measured on self-control, ways of handling feelings, and ways of coping with stress. Students who enjoyed hard thinking more also scored better on almost all of these.

claim: People who started with higher vocabulary scores gained more on the puzzles, and people who started with higher puzzle scores gained more in vocabulary.
post: Teenagers and young adults did pattern puzzles, picking which shape completes each one, and defined words out loud. About a year and a half later, most did both again. People who started with higher vocabulary scores gained more on the puzzles, and people who started with higher puzzle scores gained more in vocabulary.

claim: People felt more connected after holding the warm pack than after holding the ball.
post: While lying in a brain scanner, people held a warm pack in one round and a ball in another. Afterward they rated how connected they felt to other people. People felt more connected after holding the warm pack than after holding the ball.

claim: Scores on both lasting traits and passing mood tracked depression level, but only changes in mood tracked changes in depression, not lasting traits.
post: Adults with recurring depression filled out a long true-false personality questionnaire near the start and again at the end of about three months of talk therapy. Their depression was also rated at both times. Scores on both lasting traits and passing mood tracked depression level, but only changes in mood tracked changes in depression, not lasting traits.

claim: On the whole, patients' improvement got slightly smaller the more experience a therapist had.
post: Researchers followed 170 therapists as they treated thousands of patients over several years. Patients filled out the same symptom questionnaire before and after treatment, so each therapist's results could be tracked as they gained experience. On the whole, patients' improvement got slightly smaller the more experience a therapist had.

claim: In a new group, the estimates matched real scores with correlations of .76 and .74, and ran neither too high nor too low.
post: Psychiatric patients took a short IQ test and a longer standard one. A formula built on one group turned short-test scores into age-adjusted estimates of the standard score. In a new group, the estimates matched real scores with correlations of .76 and .74, and ran neither too high nor too low.

claim: Those who had were less likely to report theft, assault, or an arrest for a property or violent crime.
post: Adults across the US answered a government survey about their drug use and any crimes in the past year. Some had ever used psychedelics such as magic mushrooms, and others had not. Those who had were less likely to report theft, assault, or an arrest for a property or violent crime.

claim: Photos of babies and of animals showed the left side of the face more often than the right.
post: Photos of human babies and of animals were checked for which side of the face pointed toward the camera. Portraits of adults usually show the person's left cheek. Photos of babies and of animals showed the left side of the face more often than the right.

claim: Matching predicted the woman's sexual satisfaction with her partner, but whether she used it now did not.
post: Couples filled out a survey that asked about the woman's hormonal birth control, both now and when the couple first got together. For some women, use now matched use back then, and for others it had changed. Matching predicted the woman's sexual satisfaction with her partner, but whether she used it now did not.

claim: When the blue background appeared, people did better if the sorting key matched the one in the sentence than if it did not.
post: People memorized a sentence like "To make the screen blue, I have to press the left key." Then they sorted letters into vowels and consonants with the left and right keys, and the background sometimes turned blue. When the blue background appeared, people did better if the sorting key matched the one in the sentence than if it did not.

claim: People who did more of their homework also did better.
post: People in cognitive and behavioral therapy, a kind of talk therapy, were either given homework to do between sessions or not. Pooling 27 studies, therapy with homework led to better results than therapy without it. People who did more of their homework also did better.

claim: About three-quarters of the students said they would rather see a counsellor at their school.
post: Students at four Scottish secondary schools filled out a questionnaire. It asked where they would rather see a counsellor: at their school, or outside it, such as at a youth centre or doctor's office. About three-quarters of the students said they would rather see a counsellor at their school.

claim: Women who picked more negative information were more likely to expect parenthood to go badly.
post: First-time pregnant women filled out questions about how much they worried and what they expected parenthood to be like. They also chose which information about parenthood to read, positive or negative. Women who picked more negative information were more likely to expect parenthood to go badly.

claim: Sound in the left ear disrupted memory more than sound in the right ear or both ears.
post: People tried to remember a list of items in order while sounds that had nothing to do with the task played. The sounds were speech or tones, played to the left ear, the right ear, or both ears. Sound in the left ear disrupted memory more than sound in the right ear or both ears.

claim: At 13 months, babies looked longer at the object named by a known word than when the mother said a nonsense word.
post: Babies sat in front of an apparatus with an object in each of its four corners. Their mothers, who couldn't see where the baby looked, said a word the baby probably knew, a word the baby probably didn't know, or a nonsense word. At 13 months, babies looked longer at the object named by a known word than when the mother said a nonsense word.

claim: Afterward, people who sat upright reported higher self-esteem, more arousal, better mood, and less fear than people who sat slumped.
post: People sat with their backs strapped with tape, so they stayed either slumped or upright. While held in that posture, they gave a stressful speech. Afterward, people who sat upright reported higher self-esteem, more arousal, better mood, and less fear than people who sat slumped.

claim: Patients with severe alcohol problems said the other person had meant harm more than the healthy people did.
post: People read short stories about social situations that went badly, where it was not clear whether the other person meant any harm. Some of the readers were patients being treated for severe alcohol problems, and others were healthy people matched to them. Patients with severe alcohol problems said the other person had meant harm more than the healthy people did.

claim: Right after the class, girls whose teachers taught it felt better about their bodies than girls who had usual lessons.
post: Students aged 11 to 13 in British schools either had their usual lessons or took a 90-minute class on body image. Some classes were taught by their own teachers and others by researchers. Right after the class, girls whose teachers taught it felt better about their bodies than girls who had usual lessons.

claim: The three kinds of scores were clearly linked to each other.
post: Hospital patients looked at inkblots and said what they saw. Researchers scored how the figures in those blots related to each other. They scored each patient's written life story and ratings from ward staff for the same quality. The three kinds of scores were clearly linked to each other.

claim: The older the students were, the more likely they were to draw invisible sources of radiation, like nuclear power plants or mobile phones.
post: Students in grades 4 to 6 at seven schools were asked to draw a picture related to the word "radiation." Some also answered a few interview questions about their drawings. The researchers compared the drawings of younger and older students. The older the students were, the more likely they were to draw invisible sources of radiation, like nuclear power plants or mobile phones.

claim: Students scored almost 5% higher on exams after using one of the three ways than during the comparison times.
post: Students in a college psychology class took turns answering review questions in three ways: with clickers, by holding up response cards, or by raising their hands. At other times the class did none of these, as a comparison. Students scored almost 5% higher on exams after using one of the three ways than during the comparison times.

claim: People collected gems more often when the reward was immediate than when it was delayed.
post: People played an online gem game, learning by trial and error which gems to collect and which to leave. Some gems paid a small reward right away, others a larger one later, matched to be equally appealing. People collected gems more often when the reward was immediate than when it was delayed.

claim: Agents who focused more on gains made more sales, while agents who focused more on avoiding losses made fewer.
post: New sales agents answered questions about their mindset before they started the job. Some focused more on chasing gains and opportunities, and others focused more on avoiding mistakes and losses. Then researchers counted how many sales each agent made. Agents who focused more on gains made more sales, while agents who focused more on avoiding losses made fewer.

claim: More anxious children were pickier eaters, and this link was fully explained by the children's sensitivity.
post: Parents filled out questionnaires about their child's picky eating, their child's anxiety, and how sensitive their child was to things in the surroundings. More anxious children were pickier eaters, and this link was fully explained by the children's sensitivity.

claim: People with extensive training did not show more habit-like behavior than people with short training.
post: People practiced a computer task where their actions earned rewards. Some got a short amount of training and others got extensive training. Then the researchers checked whether people kept going for a reward that had lost its value, a sign of habit. People with extensive training did not show more habit-like behavior than people with short training.

claim: Kids with above-average support from both their mother and their most supportive classmate had higher self-esteem than kids with above-average support from only one of them.
post: Sixth graders were interviewed about the people in their lives and rated how supportive each person was. They also reported their own self-esteem. Kids with above-average support from both their mother and their most supportive classmate had higher self-esteem than kids with above-average support from only one of them.
journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships

claim: People whose answers were more complex, with more parts of the blot pulled together, stopped their gaze more times.
post: Adults looked at Rorschach inkblots and said what they saw, while a camera tracked their eyes. The researchers counted how many times each person's gaze stopped on the blots. People whose answers were more complex, with more parts of the blot pulled together, stopped their gaze more times.

claim: The nonstudent adults did not show this pattern.
post: College students and adults who were not students reacted to a partner's sexual unfaithfulness and to a partner's emotional unfaithfulness. Then the two kinds were compared for men and women. Among college students, men were more bothered by the sexual kind and women by the emotional kind. The nonstudent adults did not show this pattern.

claim: When a word got just one look, readers' eyes landed nearer the beginning of words with uninformative endings than of words with informative endings.
post: Skilled readers read sentences while a device tracked where their eyes landed, and then they answered questions about what they read. The sentences contained ten-letter words, some with endings that give little clue to the word, and others with informative endings. When a word got just one look, readers' eyes landed nearer the beginning of words with uninformative endings than of words with informative endings.
journal: The Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology Section A

claim: They said it improved their knowledge about mental health and mental illness and lowered their stigma toward them.
post: Students at a Canadian university read a life-skills guide for college students that had mental health information built into it. Afterward they filled out a survey, in person or online, about what the guide had done for them. They said it improved their knowledge about mental health and mental illness and lowered their stigma toward them.

claim: Only those whose self-control had been used up became more likely to start before the signal.
post: Athletes with no track experience did sprint starts, once before and once after a first task. For some, the first task was meant to use up self-control, and for others it was not. Only those whose self-control had been used up became more likely to start before the signal.

claim: That feeling predicted following health advice and helping others better than the other factors measured.
post: People worldwide took an online survey early in the COVID-19 pandemic. They said how likely they were to follow health advice, and what they would do in dilemmas like donating face masks. They also rated how connected they feel to all humanity. That feeling predicted following health advice and helping others better than the other factors measured.

claim: Half the counselors told him a positive result would mean he was 100% certain to be infected, though for a man like him the chance could be as low as 50%.
post: A researcher with low-risk behavior visited 20 public health centers in Germany as a client. At each, he sat through the counseling and took an HIV test. Half the counselors told him a positive result would mean he was 100% certain to be infected, though for a man like him the chance could be as low as 50%.

claim: Blood pressure came back to normal faster in women who got an apology than in women who didn't, but slower in men who got one than in men who didn't.
post: People did a hard subtraction task while the experimenter made harsh comments about how they were doing. Afterward, about half got an apology from the experimenter and half did not. Blood pressure came back to normal faster in women who got an apology than in women who didn't, but slower in men who got one than in men who didn't.

claim: Three broad types of problems explained the pattern well, but one general dimension behind all of them explained it even better.
post: People born in one New Zealand city were interviewed five times, from age 18 to 38, about symptoms of mental disorders like depression, phobias, and drug dependence. Researchers compared two ways of grouping the symptoms. Three broad types of problems explained the pattern well, but one general dimension behind all of them explained it even better.

claim: English speakers remembered the vowel series better than the consonant series, in both languages, but Arabic speakers did not.
post: People who spoke English as a first language and people who spoke Arabic as a first language heard series of six short syllables, each a consonant plus a vowel. They wrote down what they remembered, in both English and Arabic. English speakers remembered the vowel series better than the consonant series, in both languages, but Arabic speakers did not.

claim: Those who more easily felt positive emotions had the biggest drop in anxiety symptoms, and had fewer symptoms at the end.
post: People with panic disorder or constant worry went to ten weekly one-on-one therapy sessions that taught them to handle anxiety. Before starting, they filled out a questionnaire on how easily they feel positive emotions. Those who more easily felt positive emotions had the biggest drop in anxiety symptoms, and had fewer symptoms at the end.

claim: In every country, situations that earned more positive views from others also brought more pride.
post: People in 16 countries read 25 short situations, like being trustworthy or having many unique skills. Some rated how positively they would view another person in each situation. Others rated how much pride they would feel in it. In every country, situations that earned more positive views from others also brought more pride.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: During withdrawal, people higher in neuroticism (a tendency to worry), with less schooling, or with lower quality of life felt more distress.
post: People with anxiety or insomnia reported their distress and quality of life. Some were being weaned off calming pills, some still took them, and some had not started treatment. During withdrawal, people higher in neuroticism (a tendency to worry), with less schooling, or with lower quality of life felt more distress.

claim: Responses to the metaphor pairs were no faster than responses to the random pairs.
post: People saw pairs of words and quickly decided whether they were real words. Some pairs came from clear, sensible metaphors, some were words people tend to link in their minds, and some were randomly matched. Responses to the metaphor pairs were no faster than responses to the random pairs.

claim: Only the people in the disruptive, negative condition felt more nostalgic than the other two groups.
post: People were led to feel that their life had changed in one of three ways: a disruptive change for the worse, a non-disruptive change for the better, or no change at all. Afterward, everyone rated how nostalgic they felt. Only the people in the disruptive, negative condition felt more nostalgic than the other two groups.

claim: People on alcohol who had the memory task were less aggressive than people on alcohol without it, even less than the placebo group.
post: People took turns giving and getting mild electric shocks with an opponent who was not real. Some had alcohol and some got a placebo, and some also had to hold four things in order in memory. People on alcohol who had the memory task were less aggressive than people on alcohol without it, even less than the placebo group.

claim: People remembered faces worse when they had studied them under threat of shock, whether or not they were threatened during the recall test.
post: People studied sets of faces on a computer, then tried to recognize them. Some faces were studied while a warning said they might get an electric shock to the wrist, and others while a warning said they were safe. People remembered faces worse when they had studied them under threat of shock, whether or not they were threatened during the recall test.

claim: Symptoms of dissociation, such as seeming spaced out or detached, formed a separate group from other trauma symptoms, such as being on edge.
post: Caregivers filled out a behavior checklist about preschoolers. Some of the children were in foster care after being maltreated, and others lived at home with no known maltreatment. Symptoms of dissociation, such as seeming spaced out or detached, formed a separate group from other trauma symptoms, such as being on edge.

claim: Twenty-five of the proteins were at different levels in women with anorexia than in healthy women.
post: Women gave blood samples: some currently had anorexia, some had recovered from it, and some were healthy at a normal weight. A lab measured 92 proteins linked to inflammation in each sample. Twenty-five of the proteins were at different levels in women with anorexia than in healthy women.

claim: Treating anxiety as its own kind, apart from depression and grief, fit the answers better than using one or two kinds.
post: Older adults who had lost a husband or wife in the past six months reported their symptoms of anxiety, depression, and grief, then did so again later. Researchers compared ways of sorting those symptoms into one, two, or three kinds. Treating anxiety as its own kind, apart from depression and grief, fit the answers better than using one or two kinds.

claim: Both programs reduced eating disorder risk factors, but eight months later cognitive dissonance generally had done better.
post: New sorority members were randomly put into one of two short programs, each held over two sessions and led by fellow undergraduates. One program used cognitive dissonance, which works on the discomfort of acting against your own beliefs. The other used media advocacy. Both programs reduced eating disorder risk factors, but eight months later cognitive dissonance generally had done better.

claim: People who dwelled more intensely in that first session had higher depression scores from their clinician later in treatment.
post: Trained students watched recordings of people with depression in their first therapy session. They rated how intensely each person dwelled on their problems in a repetitive, negative, passive way. People who dwelled more intensely in that first session had higher depression scores from their clinician later in treatment.

claim: But better grades in one subject led to less confidence in the other.
post: Students were followed from fifth to eighth grade, with their math and verbal grades, and how capable they felt in each subject, recorded three times. Doing well and feeling capable in a subject led to better grades and more confidence in that same subject later. But better grades in one subject led to less confidence in the other.

claim: By the end, the first group's eating disorder risk factors and bulimic symptoms had dropped more than in the other three.
post: Teen girls unhappy with their bodies were randomly put into one of four groups. Two groups got three weekly sessions: one challenged the idea that thin is ideal, the other taught healthy weight habits. The rest did writing sessions or were only assessed. By the end, the first group's eating disorder risk factors and bulimic symptoms had dropped more than in the other three.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: Infants bounced in sync with the experimenter were more likely to help.
post: Infants were held and gently bounced to music while facing an experimenter, who bounced either in sync or out of sync with the infant. Then the experimenter 'accidentally' dropped objects, and researchers watched whether the infants handed them back. Infants bounced in sync with the experimenter were more likely to help.

claim: In resting brain scans, the therapy group's middle-back and right-front brain areas worked less in sync than before.
post: Teens who had been depressed before, but were now well or nearly well, either had weekly therapy for eight weeks or only filled out questionnaires. The therapy taught them to notice when they were dwelling on bad thoughts and to switch to something else. In resting brain scans, the therapy group's middle-back and right-front brain areas worked less in sync than before.

claim: Right after the sessions, the memory group scored higher than the waiting group.
post: Young adults were randomly split into two groups. One group had three sessions of recalling positive memories and thinking about them, while the other waited its turn. Everyone rated their self-esteem, confidence in handling stress, sense of meaning in life, and optimism. Right after the sessions, the memory group scored higher than the waiting group.

claim: Anger was judged to be stronger when the benefit was small.
post: People were asked how angry someone would get after another person harmed them. In some cases the person who did the harm gained only a small benefit from it, and in others the benefit was larger. Anger was judged to be stronger when the benefit was small.

claim: People who watched the after-course video rated his communication higher than people who watched the before-course video.
post: People went online and watched a video of one man with a stutter in a mock job interview, then rated how well he communicated. Half saw a video of him before a course on communication skills, and half saw him after it. People who watched the after-course video rated his communication higher than people who watched the before-course video.

claim: Students who believed this more strongly showed a bigger link between a higher grade in one subject and a lower self-rating in the other.
post: Students reported their math and German grades and how good they felt at each subject. They also rated whether being good at math goes with being weak at language. Students who believed this more strongly showed a bigger link between a higher grade in one subject and a lower self-rating in the other.

claim: People who put more priority on positivity felt more positive emotions and had fewer signs of depression.
post: Adults from the community filled out online surveys. One asked how much they seek out positive feelings when deciding how to organize their days. Others asked how often they felt joy, sadness and similar emotions, and how depressed they felt. People who put more priority on positivity felt more positive emotions and had fewer signs of depression.

claim: People with panic disorder named more bad experiences than the comparison group, but not fewer good ones.
post: People with panic disorder, people with depression, and people with neither were each given time periods as prompts. They named good and bad experiences from their past or ones they expected in the future. People with panic disorder named more bad experiences than the comparison group, but not fewer good ones.

claim: People who went past the limits, such as gambling more than two to three times a month, were more likely to report harm from gambling.
post: Adults across Canada answered an interview about how often they gambled, how much money they spent on it, and whether it had caused them problems. Researchers then compared people who gambled within certain limits with people who went past them. People who went past the limits, such as gambling more than two to three times a month, were more likely to report harm from gambling.

claim: Compared with when they started, the patients had improved on every measure by the end of the follow-up year.
post: Thirty people with borderline personality disorder went to therapy twice a week for a year. Their therapists were trainees who were closely supervised. Researchers tracked things like drug use, doctor visits, self-harm, hospital stays and symptoms. Compared with when they started, the patients had improved on every measure by the end of the follow-up year.

claim: People rated themselves higher on skills where they thought most others were good, and lower where they thought most others were bad.
post: People rated how good they were, from 0 to 100, at skills like driving, shoe tying, performing magic tricks and dancing. For each skill they also said whether most people are good at it, most are bad, or whether people are mixed. People rated themselves higher on skills where they thought most others were good, and lower where they thought most others were bad.
journal: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes

claim: Higher overall personality scores went with higher attractiveness, whether self-rated or rated by others.
post: People in a large national survey rated how attractive they were, and outside raters also scored how attractive each person looked. Each person also got one overall personality score, combining how their traits tend to go together. Higher overall personality scores went with higher attractiveness, whether self-rated or rated by others.

claim: Four modes (Healthy Adult, Vulnerable Child, Impulsive Child, Avoidant Protector) predicted how severe their symptoms were later.
post: People with long-standing personality problems got one of three treatments: schema therapy, another talk therapy, or their usual care. Over three years they repeatedly filled out questionnaires on how often they felt and acted in certain ways, called modes, and on their symptoms. Four modes (Healthy Adult, Vulnerable Child, Impulsive Child, Avoidant Protector) predicted how severe their symptoms were later.

claim: People were more accurate at detecting changes, and held more items in short-term memory, when their hands were near the display.
post: People did a task of spotting changes in a display while holding both hands either near the display or away from it. People were more accurate at detecting changes, and held more items in short-term memory, when their hands were near the display.

claim: People falsely said they remembered the later moments.
post: People looked at photos of someone about to do something, like an action just before it happens. Three days later they saw more photos and said which ones they had seen before. Some were old photos, and some were new photos showing a later moment of the same action. People falsely said they remembered the later moments.

claim: After reaching, they tracked where it was.
post: Babies watched videos of a woman who either reached for a toy or greeted them with "Hi baby!" and pointed at it. The toy was then hidden and came back unchanged, moved, or swapped for a different toy. After greetings, babies tracked what the toy was at the expense of where it was. After reaching, they tracked where it was.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: Fighters who looked more aggressive had won a larger share of their fights, once the fighters' weight was taken into account.
post: People looked at photos of the faces of mixed-martial-arts fighters and rated how aggressive each fighter looked. Researchers then compared those ratings with each fighter's real record of fights won. Fighters who looked more aggressive had won a larger share of their fights, once the fighters' weight was taken into account.

claim: Compared with the unrelated drumming, the matching sound helped people name the picture, and the related animal sound slowed them down.
post: People named pictures out loud, like a picture of a horse, while a sound played that they were told to ignore. The sound could match the picture (neighing), come from a related animal (barking), or have nothing to do with it (drumming). Compared with the unrelated drumming, the matching sound helped people name the picture, and the related animal sound slowed them down.
journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

claim: Students who read the culturally adapted version understood the story better than those who read the original.
post: Students learning English read a short story. Some read the original, and others read a version changed to fit their own culture. Within each group, some also did reading activities and some did not. Students who read the culturally adapted version understood the story better than those who read the original.

claim: The easily distracted, restless children had a more immature vocabulary, with more of the simpler, earlier kinds of words, than the other groups.
post: Toddlers at day-care centers were assessed for temperament. Based on this, the children fell into three groups: typical, easily distracted and restless, or shy in new situations. Then the researchers looked at how each group used words. The easily distracted, restless children had a more immature vocabulary, with more of the simpler, earlier kinds of words, than the other groups.

claim: They stayed on task more during the program than before it.
post: Six city classrooms tried a program that taught students polite ways to ask for attention or a short break. Students also worked in teams that shared rewards for good behavior. Whole classes were compared before the program and during it. They stayed on task more during the program than before it.

claim: The people who saw the chunked version did better on all the learning tests than those who saw the continuous clip.
post: Prospective teachers learned about seven teaching skills, then watched a video or animation of an expert teacher using them. Some saw it as one continuous clip. Others saw it broken into smaller chunks. The people who saw the chunked version did better on all the learning tests than those who saw the continuous clip.

claim: After three months, the children who started right away had improved more in trauma symptoms and anxiety than the children still waiting.
post: Elementary school children who had lived through frightening events joined a 10-session group program led by school clinicians, where they learned ways to cope with their feelings. Some started right away, and others waited three months first. After three months, the children who started right away had improved more in trauma symptoms and anxiety than the children still waiting.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: People remembered more words that were in a place that clashed with their meaning (positive words low, negative words high) than words in a place that matched.
post: People read a list of words one at a time, each shown in the top half or the bottom half of a computer screen. Some words were positive and some were negative. Afterward they tried to remember the words. People remembered more words that were in a place that clashed with their meaning (positive words low, negative words high) than words in a place that matched.

claim: Averaging the quick ratings did not predict what others said any better than the general rating already did.
post: People rated their own personality in two ways: one general rating, and many quick ratings of how they were acting and feeling at the moment. Other people also described each person. Averaging the quick ratings did not predict what others said any better than the general rating already did.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: When rewards came more often overall, the pigeons split their responses and their time more evenly between the keys than when rewards came less often.
post: Six pigeons could choose between two keys. Both keys paid off equally often, but one gave longer rewards than the other. When rewards came more often overall, the pigeons split their responses and their time more evenly between the keys than when rewards came less often.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: Scampia children did better than Pozzuoli children on both short-term memory and working memory (holding information in mind while using it).
post: Children in Naples, Italy, did memory tasks that used social material rather than abstract items. Some lived in two high-stress areas, Scampia and a Roma camp, and others in a lower-stress area, Pozzuoli. Scampia children did better than Pozzuoli children on both short-term memory and working memory (holding information in mind while using it).

claim: Which therapist they saw explained 12.6% of the differences in who quit and 10.1% in who got worse, after accounting for patients' own traits.
post: People went to one-on-one therapy at UK counseling services, each seeing one of 85 therapists, and filled out a questionnaire about how they felt before and after. Some quit early and some got worse. Which therapist they saw explained 12.6% of the differences in who quit and 10.1% in who got worse, after accounting for patients' own traits.

claim: Those groups tended to do better at quitting or cutting back in the short term than groups without the exercises.
post: People who smoked joined group programs to quit. In half the groups, members also did bonding exercises, like making agreements and practicing sharing personal things and giving feedback. Those groups tended to do better at quitting or cutting back in the short term than groups without the exercises.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: The thinking style that mistakes imagined danger for real danger predicted symptoms more strongly than the other styles measured.
post: People filled out questionnaires about how they think, including how much danger they expect and how much they feel their thoughts must be controlled. They also rated their obsessive-compulsive symptoms. The thinking style that mistakes imagined danger for real danger predicted symptoms more strongly than the other styles measured.

claim: The more of these symptoms parents reported, the more anxious the children rated themselves.
post: Children with anxiety disorders filled out a questionnaire about how anxious they felt. Their mothers and fathers each filled out one about their own depression, anxiety, and stress. The more of these symptoms parents reported, the more anxious the children rated themselves.
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Psychology

claim: The more people valued being happy, the more depression symptoms they reported.
post: People who had recovered from depression, but had been depressed at least three times before, filled out an online survey. It asked how much they agreed with statements like "Feeling happy is extremely important to me," and how many signs of depression they felt now. The more people valued being happy, the more depression symptoms they reported.
journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology

claim: Teenagers with two copies of the Val version of the BDNF gene reported more brooding than other teenagers, but younger children showed no such difference.
post: Children and teenagers answered questions about what they do when they feel sad. Their genes were also checked. Teenagers with two copies of the Val version of the BDNF gene reported more brooding than other teenagers, but younger children showed no such difference.

claim: Emotion changed how much people cooperated with the generous player, but made no difference with the extortion player.
post: People played a points game with another player, choosing project green to cooperate or project blue to put themselves first. The other player used either a generous strategy or a greedy extortion strategy, and showed either a cooperative or a competitive emotion. Emotion changed how much people cooperated with the generous player, but made no difference with the extortion player.

claim: People who scored higher on those traits were somewhat more likely to cope with shame by turning it outward, onto others.
post: College students filled out one questionnaire about selfish, uncaring, and impulsive personality traits, and another about how they cope with feeling ashamed. Then the two sets of scores were compared. People who scored higher on those traits were somewhat more likely to cope with shame by turning it outward, onto others.

claim: The formal requests were more effective at getting the information than the informal asks.
post: Parish councils in England were sent requests for information, some as formal Freedom of Information requests and others as simple informal asks. The formal requests were more effective at getting the information than the informal asks.
journal: Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory

claim: Depending on where it came from, a warning could be understood at grade 2.8 or needed postgraduate education.
post: The rights warnings that police read to suspects before questioning were collected from all over the US, 560 in all. Each was scored for how hard it is to read, using a school grade level. Depending on where it came from, a warning could be understood at grade 2.8 or needed postgraduate education.

claim: Creativity measures explained part of the exam scores (18%) beyond what grades and personality already explained.
post: Australian students did tasks and questionnaires that measured their creativity, such as thinking up different uses for things and writing a math equation. Researchers also collected their personality scores, school grades and national college-entry exam scores. Creativity measures explained part of the exam scores (18%) beyond what grades and personality already explained.
journal: Psychology of Aesthetics Creativity and the Arts

claim: Recall was better after sleep than after being awake, and the gap was even bigger when interference was added.
post: People learned verbal material and were tested after a period of sleep or a period awake. Some were also exposed to interference before the test. Recall was better after sleep than after being awake, and the gap was even bigger when interference was added.

claim: They recognized fewer faces correctly when the threat came during studying than when they were safe.
post: People studied faces on a screen, then picked out which ones they had seen among new faces. Sometimes they were under threat of an electric shock while studying, and sometimes they were safe. They recognized fewer faces correctly when the threat came during studying than when they were safe.

claim: When people had heard several different accented speakers during training, their adjustment to the accent carried over to the new speaker.
post: Native English speakers listened to English spoken with a Chinese accent. Then they heard sentences from a new speaker with a Chinese accent, someone they had never heard before. When people had heard several different accented speakers during training, their adjustment to the accent carried over to the new speaker.

claim: Among men, the more self-defeating traits they had, the more they remembered both their mother and their father as overinvolved.
post: Adults filled out a questionnaire about self-defeating habits, such as acting in ways that work against their own interests. They also answered a questionnaire about how they remembered their parents raising them. Among men, the more self-defeating traits they had, the more they remembered both their mother and their father as overinvolved.

claim: People who felt more grateful over the past week had a lower top-number blood pressure reaction to the stress than people who felt less grateful.
post: People rated how grateful they felt over the past week and in general. Then their heart rate and blood pressure were tracked during a stress test. People who felt more grateful over the past week had a lower top-number blood pressure reaction to the stress than people who felt less grateful.

claim: All four kinds of fixes increased those chances, compared with before.
post: Supervisors at an autism clinic filled out a checklist on why therapists rarely gave children chances to practice speaking skills. Each therapist then got a fix the checklist pointed to, like a graph of her own performance. All four kinds of fixes increased those chances, compared with before.

claim: The more narcissistic patients reported more problems getting along with other people than the less narcissistic patients did.
post: Patients admitted to a day treatment program for mental health problems filled out questionnaires about narcissism, problems in their relationships, and general distress. Researchers sorted them into high, medium, and low narcissism groups. The more narcissistic patients reported more problems getting along with other people than the less narcissistic patients did.

claim: Scanning circles, compared with all the other lines, brought extra activity in the right upper-back part of the brain.
post: People in a brain scanner scanned lines on a screen from left to right, pressing a button whenever they spotted a ring with a gap. Some lines were text, others were rows of circles instead of letters. Scanning circles, compared with all the other lines, brought extra activity in the right upper-back part of the brain.

claim: The person using strategies was rated lower in self-control than the person using willpower.
post: People read about a made-up person. Some read that the person used strategies to keep themselves in check, and others read that the person just used willpower. Then everyone rated how much self-control that person had. The person using strategies was rated lower in self-control than the person using willpower.

claim: Every student learned faster with the cards than with the worksheet.
post: College students learned to read the numbers 1 to 10 in languages they didn't know, like Mandarin and Hindi. With one teaching method, they saw one number at a time on a card. With the other, they read numbers off a worksheet as fast as they could. Every student learned faster with the cards than with the worksheet.
journal: Single Case in the Social Sciences

claim: Faces altered to be wider or more masculine were seen as more aggressive than the other versions.
post: People looked at male and female faces that had been digitally altered. Some faces were made wider compared to their height, and some were made look more masculine. People judged how aggressive each face seemed. Faces altered to be wider or more masculine were seen as more aggressive than the other versions.

claim: If cortisol rose, a testosterone rise went with lower earnings and poorer relationships.
post: People negotiated face to face, or played a bargaining game in a lab, while changes in their testosterone and cortisol (a stress hormone) were measured. When testosterone rose, people earned more and had better relationships, but only if cortisol dropped. If cortisol rose, a testosterone rise went with lower earnings and poorer relationships.

claim: The gap between men and women was biggest for a one-night fling, where men's minimum standards were lower than women's.
post: Male and female college students filled out a list of 24 traits, such as those you might want in a partner. For each kind of relationship, from a casual date to marriage to a one-night fling, they marked the lowest level they would accept. The gap between men and women was biggest for a one-night fling, where men's minimum standards were lower than women's.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Students remembered playing with friends or siblings more often than playing alone.
post: University students were asked to remember a favorite play experience from their childhood, draw it, and talk about it. Researchers then sorted what they described, including who they played with. Students remembered playing with friends or siblings more often than playing alone.

claim: Early body regulation predicted self-control partly through stress handling and attention, and the heart measure also linked directly to each later kind of regulation.
post: Babies born early had their heart-based calming and sleep cycles measured at birth. They were watched for stress reactions as infants and attention as toddlers, then tested on self-control at age 5. Early body regulation predicted self-control partly through stress handling and attention, and the heart measure also linked directly to each later kind of regulation.

claim: Interest in science predicted test scores more strongly in richer countries and richer families.
post: Teenagers around the world, about 400,000 of them in 57 countries, took a two-hour science test. They also answered questions about how much they enjoy science. Researchers compared students from richer and poorer countries and families. Interest in science predicted test scores more strongly in richer countries and richer families.

claim: People felt more grateful when the helper had kind intentions, but felt equally indebted either way.
post: People read about a favor done for them, either for kind reasons or for ulterior motives. Then they rated how grateful and how indebted they felt. People felt more grateful when the helper had kind intentions, but felt equally indebted either way.

claim: People who saw willpower as not limited did not show worse self-control afterward, unlike people who saw it as limited.
post: People said whether they think willpower is a limited resource that runs out or not. Then they went through an experience meant to use up their self-control, and their self-control was measured afterward. People who saw willpower as not limited did not show worse self-control afterward, unlike people who saw it as limited.

claim: An evaluation of the program found that schoolwork improved for both the teen tutors and the children they tutored.
post: Teenagers with disabilities tutored younger children with disabilities twice a week for 10 weeks, in reading, language arts, and math. School staff trained and supported the teen tutors. An evaluation of the program found that schoolwork improved for both the teen tutors and the children they tutored.

claim: The test's built-in checks for faking still worked fairly well.
post: University students filled out a personality questionnaire. Some were told to answer honestly. Others were told to answer so they made an excellent impression, and were warned that the test could catch faking, so they should try not to get caught. The test's built-in checks for faking still worked fairly well.

claim: The two groups' total scores did not differ.
post: Students were given hypnotic suggestions to respond to. For some the suggestions went from easy to difficult, and for others from difficult to easy. The two groups' total scores did not differ.
journal: International Journal of Clinical and Experimental Hypnosis

claim: Every child seemed to react to a sound twice: once when it happened, and again after a delay of up to a second.
post: Children were filmed with sound, some with severe autistic-like difficulties and others with milder reading problems. The films were then studied in tiny slices of time. Every child seemed to react to a sound twice: once when it happened, and again after a delay of up to a second.
journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

claim: People who got oxytocin were more trusting that their privacy would not be violated.
post: People were randomly given oxytocin or a placebo and were asked to trust someone with confidential information. People who got oxytocin were more trusting that their privacy would not be violated.

claim: Bodily and sensory states were said to stop, but feelings, wants and knowing things were said to continue.
post: People with different beliefs about life after death were interviewed about a person who had died. They were asked whether various things in that person's mind and body would still go on after death. Bodily and sensory states were said to stop, but feelings, wants and knowing things were said to continue.

claim: Closer, calmer families went with a later first period in women with two copies of the rarer version of that gene, but not in other women.
post: Women rated how close and how full of conflict their childhood family was, and said when they got their first period. Their DNA was checked for a gene that responds to estrogen. Closer, calmer families went with a later first period in women with two copies of the rarer version of that gene, but not in other women.

claim: Mothers with the A-A or A-G version of an oxytocin receptor gene were rated less sensitive to their toddlers than mothers with G-G.
post: Mothers and their 2-year-olds did tasks like free play and puzzles, while observers rated how supportive each mother was. The mothers also gave cheek swabs for a gene test. Mothers with the A-A or A-G version of an oxytocin receptor gene were rated less sensitive to their toddlers than mothers with G-G.

claim: The people who rewrote the image were more willing to carry out the test.
post: People thought of a social situation they feared and planned a small real-life test of their worst-case belief about it. Half then did an exercise where they imagined the feared moment and rewrote it in their minds. The other half just took a break. The people who rewrote the image were more willing to carry out the test.

claim: Those who scored high on both reported more severe OCD symptoms than the other groups, but about the same level of PTSD symptoms.
post: College students answered questions about symptoms of OCD, which involves unwanted thoughts and urges, and symptoms of PTSD, which follows a traumatic event. Some scored high enough for probable OCD, some for probable PTSD, and some for both. Those who scored high on both reported more severe OCD symptoms than the other groups, but about the same level of PTSD symptoms.
journal: The Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease

claim: After the lesson, the students nudged toward weak solutions showed higher-quality reasoning than those nudged toward good ones.
post: Data science students worked alone on a data puzzle before being taught the idea behind it. Some were nudged toward good solutions with hints. Others were nudged to come up with weak solutions. After the lesson, the students nudged toward weak solutions showed higher-quality reasoning than those nudged toward good ones.

claim: Accuracy on each test type shifted with its share of rewards, in a pattern a standard reward-and-choice formula described well.
post: Pigeons saw a sample that combined a color and a line tilt. After a delay, they had to match either its color or its tilt. The researchers changed how often correct answers were rewarded on color tests versus tilt tests. Accuracy on each test type shifted with its share of rewards, in a pattern a standard reward-and-choice formula described well.

claim: Those who tended to act rashly when happy craved gaming more, and that craving went with more signs of problem gaming.
post: Frequent video game players filled out questionnaires about how strongly they crave gaming and how many signs of problem gaming they had. They also answered questions about acting rashly when feeling very happy. Those who tended to act rashly when happy craved gaming more, and that craving went with more signs of problem gaming.
journal: Cyberpsychology: Journal of Psychosocial Research on Cyberspace

claim: Even after that shared distress was set aside, answers still showed a separate depression pattern and a separate anxiety pattern.
post: People getting outpatient psychiatric care and a separate group of college students filled out two checklists, one about depression symptoms and one about anxiety symptoms. Answers on the two lists overlapped because of a shared feeling of general distress. Even after that shared distress was set aside, answers still showed a separate depression pattern and a separate anxiety pattern.

claim: Young people with the diagnosis were more likely to call in-between faces angry rather than happy.
post: Young people looked at faces that had been blended step by step from clearly happy to clearly angry. For each face they had to say whether it looked happy or angry. Some of the young people had a diagnosis of severe irritability and temper outbursts, and others were healthy. Young people with the diagnosis were more likely to call in-between faces angry rather than happy.
journal: Journal of Child and Adolescent Psychopharmacology

claim: The children could not reliably tell the two French accents apart, but they could tell their own accent from the foreign one.
post: Young French-speaking children heard sentences and had to sort them by accent. Sometimes the accents were Southern and Northern French. Other times they were the children's own accent and a strong foreign accent. The children could not reliably tell the two French accents apart, but they could tell their own accent from the foreign one.

claim: The more often moderators saw distressing content, the more psychological distress and secondary trauma they reported, but their well-being did not change with it.
post: Content moderators, people whose job is to review and remove harmful posts uploaded to the internet, filled out an online survey. It asked how often they saw distressing content, and about their distress, trauma symptoms and well-being. The more often moderators saw distressing content, the more psychological distress and secondary trauma they reported, but their well-being did not change with it.

claim: Compared with Americans, East Asians were more sensitive to changes in the background than to changes in the main object.
post: American and East Asian students looked at still photos and short animated scenes. In some, something about the main object changed, and in others something in the background changed. Participants had to spot the change. Compared with Americans, East Asians were more sensitive to changes in the background than to changes in the main object.

claim: Those who learned the picture labels first responded faster than the others, in every part of the test.
post: Students learned to say a different label for each of eight pictures, and to link pairs of those labels. Half learned the picture labels first, and half learned the label pairs first. Then everyone did a test with just the pictures. Those who learned the picture labels first responded faster than the others, in every part of the test.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: The urge to do something to undo the thought faded less in people who dwelled on the thought than in the other two groups.
post: People wrote down a sentence saying they wished a loved one would die in a horrible car accident. Then some spent time dwelling on that thought, some dwelled on their bad mood, and some distracted themselves by thinking about everyday objects and situations. The urge to do something to undo the thought faded less in people who dwelled on the thought than in the other two groups.
journal: Journal of Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorders

claim: Children whose mothers were neutral after good behavior and punished bad behavior had higher fear of failure than those whose mothers rewarded good behavior and were neutral after bad.
post: Mothers filled out a questionnaire about how they reacted when their children behaved well or badly. Their children had either a high or a low fear of failure. Children whose mothers were neutral after good behavior and punished bad behavior had higher fear of failure than those whose mothers rewarded good behavior and were neutral after bad.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Students' answers on 8 of the 14 survey measures were linked to how selective their school was.
post: College students filled out a survey about the in-between stage of life after the teen years. They came from 10 schools, which the researchers ranked by what share of applicants each school turned away. Students' answers on 8 of the 14 survey measures were linked to how selective their school was.

claim: Among the children, understanding seemed to drop with age, as older children more often chose the literal meaning of some of them.
post: Preschool children and adults did a task where they had to understand made-up figures of speech, in which a word for one thing stands in for something connected to it. Adults did better overall. Among the children, understanding seemed to drop with age, as older children more often chose the literal meaning of some of them.

claim: The link was stronger in the borderline group.
post: People with borderline personality disorder or depression carried a handheld computer for 28 days. It beeped six times a day, asking how hostile, sad, or afraid they felt and whether anyone had rejected or argued with them. In both groups, rejection and arguments went with more hostility, and the reverse too. The link was stronger in the borderline group.

claim: Women preferred more masculine bodies when their fertility was likely at its highest than at other times in their cycle.
post: Women rated male bodies that varied in how masculine they looked. Some were tested at different points in their menstrual cycle, including the days when pregnancy is most likely. Women preferred more masculine bodies when their fertility was likely at its highest than at other times in their cycle.

claim: That gap was bigger in people with certain gene versions than in people without them.
post: European Americans and Asian-born Asians rated how independent or connected to others they are, and had a dopamine-related gene tested. European Americans rated themselves more independent, Asian-born Asians more connected. That gap was bigger in people with certain gene versions than in people without them.

claim: Most got the toy-fridge version right, but most failed the standard one.
post: Three-year-olds watched an experimenter move a toy girl's bananas from one toy fridge to another. Then each child moved the girl to where she would go for her bananas. The same children also did a standard version of the task. Most got the toy-fridge version right, but most failed the standard one.

claim: The problem behavior came back in 36% of the changes of person and 26% of the changes of setting.
post: Treatment for a problem behavior that is rewarding in itself was sometimes handed to a new person, like a caregiver, or moved to a new place, like the home. Past records of these changes were reviewed. The problem behavior came back in 36% of the changes of person and 26% of the changes of setting.

claim: Students with the worksheets scored higher on the second test than the first, going from 73% to 79% correct.
post: College students in some classes got reading worksheets and tutorials to help them read published research articles. Students in other classes did not. Everyone took a multiple-choice test on understanding research articles, before and after. Students with the worksheets scored higher on the second test than the first, going from 73% to 79% correct.

claim: Women who valued their appearance more at the start were more distressed across the year after surgery.
post: Women with early stage breast cancer rated how much they valued having a good physical appearance, before their surgery. Then they reported on their mood several times over the next year. Women who valued their appearance more at the start were more distressed across the year after surgery.

claim: The psychopathy and sadism questionnaires showed virtually the same pattern of links to those characteristics.
post: People filled out questionnaires, some meant to measure psychopathy and others meant to measure sadism, which is enjoying hurting others. Then each questionnaire's scores were compared with 51 other characteristics. The psychopathy and sadism questionnaires showed virtually the same pattern of links to those characteristics.

claim: While getting the lessons, children's skills grew faster in knowing about print, in rhyming, and in dropping a sound from a word.
post: Preschoolers who were at risk of struggling to read were split by chance into two groups. One group got nine weeks of small-group reading-readiness lessons in the fall, and the other got the same lessons in the spring. While getting the lessons, children's skills grew faster in knowing about print, in rhyming, and in dropping a sound from a word.

claim: Of everything measured, their confidence in teaching inclusively was most closely linked to how resilient they were.
post: Student teachers at a Finnish university filled out a survey. It asked how confident they felt about teaching classrooms that include all kinds of learners, and how well they cope with hard times. It also asked about their backgrounds. Of everything measured, their confidence in teaching inclusively was most closely linked to how resilient they were.

claim: In a part of the brain called the amygdala, people without depression reacted more to happy faces, while depressed people reacted more to sad faces.
post: People lay in a brain scanner while faces flashed on a screen for a split second, too fast to notice, with happy and sad faces mixed together. Some people were being treated in a hospital for depression, and others were not depressed. In a part of the brain called the amygdala, people without depression reacted more to happy faces, while depressed people reacted more to sad faces.

claim: Hidden knowledge was detected substantially better with the fillers than without them.
post: People took an online reaction-time test meant to detect whether someone is hiding what they know, like their own country. Questions came one detail at a time. Some people also got filler words like "KNOWN" and "UNKNOWN" mixed in; others did not. Hidden knowledge was detected substantially better with the fillers than without them.
journal: Journal of Applied Research in Memory and Cognition

claim: In poorer homes, the environment twins share explained more of the differences in scores, while in more affluent homes genes explained more.
post: Twins took a national scholastic aptitude test as teenagers in 1962, and their families' income and parents' education were noted. The twins were then compared across poorer and more affluent homes. In poorer homes, the environment twins share explained more of the differences in scores, while in more affluent homes genes explained more.

claim: Over the 10 runs, the fearful women's nervousness, sense of lost control, and body responses went down, but the other women's did not.
post: Women who were very afraid of anxious-feeling body sensations, and women who were not, each ran for 10 minutes, 10 separate times. After each run they rated how nervous they felt and how out of control. Over the 10 runs, the fearful women's nervousness, sense of lost control, and body responses went down, but the other women's did not.

claim: People who had caused harm gave more of their resources to the other person at their own expense.
post: Japanese participants imagined a scenario in which they had either caused harm to someone or not. Then they decided how to share resources between themselves and the other person. People who had caused harm gave more of their resources to the other person at their own expense.

claim: People with OCD reported more of all three than the other groups in low-risk and OCD-related situations.
post: People with OCD, people with social anxiety, and people without anxiety problems rated situations with a risk of harm. They said how much they wanted to fix each one, how upset they'd be leaving it, and how responsible they'd feel. People with OCD reported more of all three than the other groups in low-risk and OCD-related situations.

claim: The more gamers spent on loot boxes, the more severe their problem gambling.
post: Gamers found through gaming forums on reddit filled out an online survey. It asked how much money they spend each month on loot boxes, which are in-game items bought with real money that hold random contents, and how severe their gambling problems were. The more gamers spent on loot boxes, the more severe their problem gambling.

claim: The split between "met" and "blocked" needs probably came mostly from positive versus negative wording.
post: College students and some other adults filled out a questionnaire about whether their basic needs were being met or blocked. Some statements were worded positively and others negatively. The same people also answered other well-being questionnaires. The split between "met" and "blocked" needs probably came mostly from positive versus negative wording.

claim: Of the witnesses who had talked, 71% mistakenly recalled details they had only heard from their partner.
post: Pairs of people each watched a different video of the same crime, so some details appeared in only one video. Some pairs talked about the event before being tested alone, and others were not allowed to talk. Of the witnesses who had talked, 71% mistakenly recalled details they had only heard from their partner.

claim: It found five types of learners, with labels like "process-oriented competent" and "avoiding-unreflective."
post: Students training to be teachers filled out an online survey about how they set goals, study, and look back on their learning. Researchers then used a statistical method that sorts people into groups with similar answer patterns. It found five types of learners, with labels like "process-oriented competent" and "avoiding-unreflective."

claim: Partners' body sway matched most when the talk moved on and they could see each other.
post: Pairs of people made a decision together in Finnish while their body movements and voices were recorded. Sometimes they could see each other, sometimes not. The talk either moved on to a next step or just kept going. Partners' body sway matched most when the talk moved on and they could see each other.
journal: Research on Language and Social Interaction

claim: Quiz scores were higher in the interteaching weeks than in the discussion forum weeks.
