post: Therapy clients and some students filled out a personality questionnaire called the 16 PF. Researchers used the answers to predict each person's scores on personality disorder scales, then checked them against a different personality disorder test the same people took. Ten of 11 predicted scores were related to the other test's scores by more than chance.

claim: That stronger sense of connection helped them feel that their past self and present self are linked.
post: People took part in experiments on nostalgia, the sentimental longing for your own past. Nostalgia boosted people's sense of belonging and acceptance by others. That stronger sense of connection helped them feel that their past self and present self are linked.

claim: The strongest difference was at one spot in the DNA, near a gene called DISP1.
post: People with obsessive-compulsive disorder said whether a common serotonin-targeting medication had helped them. Most said it did, and some said it did not. Researchers then compared DNA across the whole genome between the two groups. The strongest difference was at one spot in the DNA, near a gene called DISP1.

claim: Those with the exposure showed less of the usual bias against believing accented speakers.
post: People listened to information spoken by native and nonnative speakers and judged how believable it was. Some first got a short exposure to foreign-accented speech, and others did not. Those with the exposure showed less of the usual bias against believing accented speakers.

claim: People defended their culture more after thinking about death than after thinking about dental pain or a self-chosen death.
post: People were asked to think about one of three things: death, a death that someone chooses for themselves, or dental pain. Then researchers measured how strongly they defended their own culture and its norms. People defended their culture more after thinking about death than after thinking about dental pain or a self-chosen death.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: How mothers guided, the home environment, and family income all helped predict the boys' resilience and improvement.
post: Mothers were videotaped giving their sons a short lesson; all the boys had a learning disability. Researchers scored how each mother guided her son, then tested the boys' resilience and how much they improved with help. How mothers guided, the home environment, and family income all helped predict the boys' resilience and improvement.

claim: After training, people showed appropriate feedback-receiving behavior and kept it up, compared with before training.
post: Employees sat through spoken feedback sessions while researchers watched how they received it. Everyone was observed first without training, then got training on how to receive feedback, starting at a different time for each person. After training, people showed appropriate feedback-receiving behavior and kept it up, compared with before training.

claim: Eight weeks later, both program groups had less depression and anxiety and better relationships than the control group.
post: Young adults in dating relationships were randomly put into three groups. One group did a computer program about their relationship, one did a computer program about handling depression and anxiety, and one was a control group. Eight weeks later, both program groups had less depression and anxiety and better relationships than the control group.
journal: Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology

claim: People with higher well-being used this more when they felt little control, and less when they felt more control.
post: People used a phone app that asked them 10 times a day for one week how much they had tried to look at their situation in a calmer, more positive way. It also asked how much control they felt they had over what was happening. People with higher well-being used this more when they felt little control, and less when they felt more control.

claim: The slow brain waves of children with dyslexia lined up with a different point in the beat than those of the other children.
post: Children with and without dyslexia heard the syllable "ba" repeated at a steady beat, twice a second, while their brain activity was recorded. They pressed a button whenever the beat was delayed. The slow brain waves of children with dyslexia lined up with a different point in the beat than those of the other children.

claim: Women with lower percent body fat were more likely to have a poor long-term outcome.
post: Women with anorexia nervosa who had recently regained a healthy weight had their body fat, body mass index and stress and appetite hormones measured. Researchers then followed them through a trial meant to prevent relapse and rated how each woman did at the end. Women with lower percent body fat were more likely to have a poor long-term outcome.

claim: Pupils were largest for the dark words, in between for neutral words, and smallest for the bright words.
post: People's pupils were measured while they read single words that conveyed brightness, such as day, darkness, such as night, or neither, such as house. Pupils were largest for the dark words, in between for neutral words, and smallest for the bright words.

claim: They did better on the words studied one day apart than on the words studied eight days apart.
post: Primary school students in Hong Kong studied 20 English adjectives in two sessions. For some words the two sessions were one day apart, and for other words they were eight days apart. Four weeks later, they took a multiple-choice test. They did better on the words studied one day apart than on the words studied eight days apart.

claim: A statistical test found strong support for the 12-theme grouping.
post: People filled out a long online survey of statements about how they handle their thoughts, feelings and daily life. The statements were pulled together from many existing questionnaires. Then the researchers checked whether the answers grouped into 12 separate themes. A statistical test found strong support for the 12-theme grouping.

claim: Children without autism, matched to the autistic children on language level, looked more at the matching video when the delay was 0.6 or 1 second.
post: Young children watched two identical videos of a woman talking, side by side, while one soundtrack played. In one video the sound matched her mouth. In the other, her mouth ran 0.3, 0.6, or 1 second ahead of the sound. Children without autism, matched to the autistic children on language level, looked more at the matching video when the delay was 0.6 or 1 second.

claim: People who had held the expansive poses performed better and were more likely to be chosen for hire.
post: People held either expansive, open poses or contracted, closed poses. Then they prepared and gave a speech to two evaluators in a mock job interview. People who had held the expansive poses performed better and were more likely to be chosen for hire.

claim: Spreading the sounds out disrupted memory less than playing them all from one spot.
post: People saw a list of seven letters on a screen, then wrote them down in order after a pause, while ignoring a looping sound of three spoken syllables in headphones. For some, all syllables came from one spot. For others, each syllable came from the left, middle, or right. Spreading the sounds out disrupted memory less than playing them all from one spot.

claim: People could successfully track twice as many objects when they were split across both sides as when they were all on one side.
post: People tried to keep track of several moving objects on a screen at once. In some cases all the objects they had to follow were on one side of the screen. In others the objects were split between the left and right sides. People could successfully track twice as many objects when they were split across both sides as when they were all on one side.

claim: People primed with low support preferred more feminine-looking faces, of both sexes, than people primed with high support.
post: Women and men were randomly assigned to be primed to think about having either low or high social support. Then they looked at faces and chose which ones they preferred. People primed with low support preferred more feminine-looking faces, of both sexes, than people primed with high support.

claim: People who read the arrival-time ranges saw the threat as more serious and were more likely to urge action than people who read the outcome ranges.
post: People read statements and looked at graphs about climate change, such as rising temperatures and sea levels. Some read a range of how bad things could be by a fixed date. Others read a range of when a fixed level of harm would arrive. People who read the arrival-time ranges saw the threat as more serious and were more likely to urge action than people who read the outcome ranges.
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences

claim: Teams that sang with more passion went on to concede fewer goals than teams that sang with less.
post: Before each game at a major European soccer tournament, the players sang their national anthems. Researchers compared how much passion each team showed while singing across the tournament's 51 games. Teams that sang with more passion went on to concede fewer goals than teams that sang with less.

claim: Learning true numbers for some countries pushed people's memory of their guesses toward the truth, even for countries whose numbers they were not shown.
post: People guessed the populations of many countries. Some were then shown the true populations for a set of countries, and later everyone tried to recall their own first guesses. Learning true numbers for some countries pushed people's memory of their guesses toward the truth, even for countries whose numbers they were not shown.

claim: What they reported doing varied from one evaluator to the next, which suggests they do not always follow the official practice guidelines.
post: Professionals who evaluate people for legal cases filled out a survey about their own work. It asked how often they use practices meant to respect the cultural background of the people they evaluate. What they reported doing varied from one evaluator to the next, which suggests they do not always follow the official practice guidelines.
journal: International Journal of Forensic Mental Health

claim: For the detailed figures, the most attractive leg length was a bit longer than average, about half a standard deviation above it.
post: Women rated how attractive male figures were, one at a time, from 1 to 7. The figures were computer-made men of the same height, but with legs that ranged from shorter to longer. Some were plain silhouettes and others were detailed figures. For the detailed figures, the most attractive leg length was a bit longer than average, about half a standard deviation above it.

claim: Mood strongly shaped their ratings of life overall, but had only a weak effect on their ratings of specific parts of life.
post: People who were in a better or worse temporary mood rated how satisfied they were with their life overall. They also rated how satisfied they were with specific parts of their life. Mood strongly shaped their ratings of life overall, but had only a weak effect on their ratings of specific parts of life.

claim: Young children who failed the spoken version were more likely to show they understood pouring doesn't change the amount, using buttons.
post: Children learned to press a button for two jars with equal water, and not press for unequal. Then one jar was poured into a differently shaped jar, and children signaled without words whether the amounts were still equal. Young children who failed the spoken version were more likely to show they understood pouring doesn't change the amount, using buttons.

claim: In sessions 6 to 10, those with more unhealthy eating attitudes gained weight more slowly than those with less unhealthy ones.
post: Adults with anorexia began a course of talking therapy. At the start, they answered questions about their eating attitudes, like restricting food and worrying about body shape, and their weight was tracked over 10 sessions. In sessions 6 to 10, those with more unhealthy eating attitudes gained weight more slowly than those with less unhealthy ones.

claim: Overall it did, but the effect was very small.
post: People tried to influence a machine that spits out random numbers, just by intending a result. Researchers pooled 380 such studies, checking whether the machine's output lined up with what people intended. Overall it did, but the effect was very small.

claim: Brain responses to the tone were weaker when it matched what that hand predicted than when it did not.
post: People pressed one of four buttons, and each press made a tone play. Sometimes the tone was the one linked to that hand, and sometimes it was a different one. Brain responses to the tone were weaker when it matched what that hand predicted than when it did not.

claim: In the non-threat condition, highly socially anxious people discounted later rewards more than people with low social anxiety, meaning they valued them less.
post: People who reported high or low social anxiety were randomly put into a social threat condition or a non-threat condition. Then they made choices between rewards now and rewards later. In the non-threat condition, highly socially anxious people discounted later rewards more than people with low social anxiety, meaning they valued them less.

claim: Men in the romantic mindset reported being more willing to take risks than men who were not.
post: Some men and women were put in the mindset of wanting to attract a romantic partner, and others were not. Then everyone said how willing they would be to take risks in several different areas of life. Men in the romantic mindset reported being more willing to take risks than men who were not.

claim: Children showed modest improvements in vocabulary and comprehension, and this repeated within and across children.
post: Nine preschoolers in public pre-K classrooms sat in small groups with headphones and listened to recorded stories. Vocabulary and comprehension lessons were built into the stories. The researchers checked each child's learning on the lesson targets. Children showed modest improvements in vocabulary and comprehension, and this repeated within and across children.

claim: Sexual satisfaction and marital satisfaction were more closely linked in longer marriages than in shorter ones.
post: Married Jewish women, religious and secular, answered an online survey about how satisfied they were with their sex lives and with their marriages. The researchers compared women in shorter marriages with women in longer ones. Sexual satisfaction and marital satisfaction were more closely linked in longer marriages than in shorter ones.

claim: In the familiar play, children who showed less joy approached less, but wariness was not related to approach.
post: Preschoolers did play activities in a lab, like racing toy cars and blowing bubbles, plus newer, scarier ones, like a stranger walking up. Researchers rated each child's joy and how wary they were of new things. In the familiar play, children who showed less joy approached less, but wariness was not related to approach.

claim: Introverts were more often born just after Saturn rose or peaked in the sky, and extraverts just after Mars and Jupiter did.
post: Birth dates and places were pulled from the biographies of famous French scientists, athletes, and actors. For each person, the sky positions of Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn at birth were worked out, and their personality descriptions were rated. Introverts were more often born just after Saturn rose or peaked in the sky, and extraverts just after Mars and Jupiter did.
journal: British Journal of Social and Clinical Psychology

claim: Poems with more burst sounds were rated pleasant and lively, and poems with more nasal sounds were rated unpleasant and low-energy.
post: People read poems and rated the mood of each one. Some poems had a lot of burst sounds like P and T, made by briefly stopping the air. Others had a lot of nasal sounds like M and N. Poems with more burst sounds were rated pleasant and lively, and poems with more nasal sounds were rated unpleasant and low-energy.

claim: Mental or behavioral ones were seen as more the person's own doing, and drew less pity, more anger, and less willingness to help than physical ones.
post: People rated 10 stigmatized conditions. For each, they judged whether the person caused it, how they felt toward the person, and whether to help. Some conditions were physical and others were mental or behavioral. Mental or behavioral ones were seen as more the person's own doing, and drew less pity, more anger, and less willingness to help than physical ones.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: In cognitive therapy, people with high self-control scores did better than people with low scores.
post: People with moderate depression were randomly given 12 weeks of either cognitive therapy, a kind of talk therapy, or an antidepressant drug. Before starting, they filled out a questionnaire on self-control skills. In cognitive therapy, people with high self-control scores did better than people with low scores.

claim: Men rated their own overall IQ higher than women rated theirs, but the two groups did not differ in how they rated their parents or siblings.
post: Students in Belgium, Britain and Slovakia estimated their own IQ scores. They also estimated the IQ of their parents and their brothers and sisters. Men rated their own overall IQ higher than women rated theirs, but the two groups did not differ in how they rated their parents or siblings.

claim: Both groups put adjectives closest to the noun, then numbers, then demonstratives like "this" or "that."
post: English speakers and Thai speakers learned a made-up language in which describing words came before or after the noun, unlike in their own language. They only practiced phrases with one describing word, then had to guess how to say phrases with several. Both groups put adjectives closest to the noun, then numbers, then demonstratives like "this" or "that."

claim: Grief symptoms formed their own cluster and barely overlapped with depression or anxiety symptoms.
post: Widowed people were interviewed about six months after their spouse went into the hospital. They answered questions about grief, depression, and anxiety symptoms. A statistical method then sorted the symptoms into clusters that go together. Grief symptoms formed their own cluster and barely overlapped with depression or anxiety symptoms.

claim: People who had seen organic foods volunteered less time.
post: People viewed a few organic foods, comfort foods, or control foods. Then they were asked to volunteer time to help a needy stranger. People who had seen organic foods volunteered less time.

claim: Pairs with different skin tones were judged less coordinated than pairs with similar skin tones.
post: People judged how well coordinated two people were with each other. Some pairs had similar skin tones and others had different skin tones, but the actual amount of coordination was the same. Pairs with different skin tones were judged less coordinated than pairs with similar skin tones.

claim: Naming was driven by how common the whole word was, not by how common its parts were.
post: People saw pictures and named each one out loud, in either Mandarin Chinese or English. The names were words built from two smaller words. Some whole words were common while their parts were rare, and others were the reverse. Naming was driven by how common the whole word was, not by how common its parts were.

claim: Those who had spent more on loot boxes were more likely to have started gambling, and to spend more on it.
post: Young adult gamers who did not gamble reported how much money they spent on loot boxes, the video game prizes you pay for without knowing what you'll get. Six months later, they said whether they had started gambling. Those who had spent more on loot boxes were more likely to have started gambling, and to spend more on it.

claim: People reminded of death identified more strongly with their group and showed more bias in favor of it.
post: Some people were reminded of their own death and others were not. Then they answered questions about a group they belonged to. People reminded of death identified more strongly with their group and showed more bias in favor of it.

claim: Compared with primes that only shared letters, a shared ending gave the word a boost, whether it came alone or inside a whole word.
post: People saw a word like WALKER and decided whether it was a real word. Just before it, a brief flash showed the ending alone ("er"), a whole word with that ending ("baker"), or an unrelated prime. Compared with primes that only shared letters, a shared ending gave the word a boost, whether it came alone or inside a whole word.

claim: While learning, people more bothered by uncertainty reacted to the safe squares too; less bothered people told the scream square apart better.
post: People watched yellow squares of four sizes while finger sensors tracked their sweat response. Either the biggest or the smallest square sometimes came with a loud scream in headphones; the other squares never did. While learning, people more bothered by uncertainty reacted to the safe squares too; less bothered people told the scream square apart better.

claim: Students told the drink would make them anxious showed a smaller brain response to errors than students given no such explanation.
post: University students drank a beverage. Some were told it would make them anxious, and others were told it would have no side effects. Then everyone did a task where they pressed a key or held back, while a cap recorded their brain's response to mistakes. Students told the drink would make them anxious showed a smaller brain response to errors than students given no such explanation.

claim: They also had lower automatic, gut-level good feelings toward it.
post: Students thought about their country and rated how much they agreed with statements like "My group is extraordinary." Their answers were compared with how they felt about their group. People who scored higher felt better about their group privately but thought others saw it less well. They also had lower automatic, gut-level good feelings toward it.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Those who rated values and not feeling ready as more important had less sexual experience.
post: Students filled out an online survey the summer before college. They rated how important reasons like moral values or not feeling ready were in deciding whether to have sex, and said whether they had ever had sex. Those who rated values and not feeling ready as more important had less sexual experience.

claim: The thinking therapy worked better than the relationship therapy for more avoidant patients, and the relationship therapy worked better for more obsessive ones.
post: Depressed patients got one of two talk therapies: one worked on thinking habits, the other on relationships. Patients also differed in how avoidant or how obsessive their personalities were. The thinking therapy worked better than the relationship therapy for more avoidant patients, and the relationship therapy worked better for more obsessive ones.
journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology

claim: Teaching at the table and inside the game were equally effective and efficient.
post: Preschool boys with autism learned to touch the picture that matched a spoken word. Some words were taught at a table with picture cards and treats. Others were taught inside a game, like a jumping game or a toy train. Teaching at the table and inside the game were equally effective and efficient.

claim: Students with higher SAT scores were not clearly less biased toward their own side than students with lower scores.
post: College students said whether they smoked, drank alcohol, or believed in God, and reported their SAT scores. Then they rated how much they agreed with a statement tied to each habit, such as "Secondhand smoke is a health hazard for nonsmokers." Students with higher SAT scores were not clearly less biased toward their own side than students with lower scores.

claim: Students who scored more Type A had higher grade point averages than students who scored less Type A.
post: Students filled out a survey that scores how hard-driving, rushed, and competitive a person is, a style called Type A. Their scores were then compared with their grades. Students who scored more Type A had higher grade point averages than students who scored less Type A.

claim: Skills for handling everyday tasks were the most connected to all the others.
post: People with schizophrenia, living in the community and stable on medication, were measured on symptoms, thinking skills, daily-life skills, and how they managed real life. Researchers mapped which measures were linked to which. Skills for handling everyday tasks were the most connected to all the others.

claim: Back in the first setting, lever pressing returned more in the switching rats than in the others.
post: Rats pressed a lever in one setting where it paid off, and in another where it did not. Some got all of the first setting, then all of the second. Others switched between the two every day. Back in the first setting, lever pressing returned more in the switching rats than in the others.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: There were slight but consistent differences in how the words sounded when read as a noun versus as a verb.
post: Five speakers were recorded reading aloud 16 words that can be either a noun or a verb, such as answer or design. Each word was read once as a noun and once as a verb. There were slight but consistent differences in how the words sounded when read as a noun versus as a verb.

claim: The hidden-cue walks felt better, were remembered and expected to be more pleasant, and felt less hard than the other three.
post: Physically active people walked briskly on a treadmill four times: with music, with a music video, with a music video hiding cues too quick to notice, and with nothing. The hidden-cue walks felt better, were remembered and expected to be more pleasant, and felt less hard than the other three.

claim: The other problems that came with developmental trauma disorder overlapped with those of PTSD but also included panic, separation anxiety, and disruptive behavior disorders.
post: Interviewers asked parents, children, or both about kids' past trauma and current symptoms. Each child was screened for developmental trauma disorder (a proposed label for lasting harm from childhood abuse or neglect), PTSD, and other disorders. The other problems that came with developmental trauma disorder overlapped with those of PTSD but also included panic, separation anxiety, and disruptive behavior disorders.

claim: Toddlers were happier giving treats to the puppets than receiving treats themselves.
post: Toddlers played with puppets that made happy "yum" noises when they got a treat. Sometimes the toddlers were asked to give treats to the puppets, and at other times they got treats themselves. Their happiness was rated each time. Toddlers were happier giving treats to the puppets than receiving treats themselves.

claim: People who watched more TV guessed that those things were more common, and they answered faster than people who watched less.
post: People answered questions about how common certain things are in real life, and the computer timed how fast they answered. They also said how much television they watch. People who watched more TV guessed that those things were more common, and they answered faster than people who watched less.

claim: On average, the children reached the learning goal in fewer sessions with examples shown together than with examples shown one after another.
post: Preschool children with developmental delays were taught to name letters or letter sounds. Some items were taught with examples shown one after another, and others with examples shown together. On average, the children reached the learning goal in fewer sessions with examples shown together than with examples shown one after another.

claim: People who had first disagreed with the sexist statements were more willing to favor the man.
post: Some people first had the chance to disagree with blatantly sexist statements, and others did not. Later they chose whether to favor a man or a woman for a stereotypically male job. People who had first disagreed with the sexist statements were more willing to favor the man.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: One setup that fit acceptably put emotional ability as a branch under general intelligence, alongside skills like reasoning and visual processing.
post: College students took tests of reasoning, knowledge, math, visual skills and memory, plus tests of noticing, understanding and handling emotions. The researchers tried several ways of organizing the scores. One setup that fit acceptably put emotional ability as a branch under general intelligence, alongside skills like reasoning and visual processing.

claim: The two groups did not differ in how often they chose the lesser verdict of diminished responsibility, which treats mental illness as partly excusing a killing.
post: People played jurors watching a filmed mock murder trial. For half, the defendant was described as having a "severe personality disorder, borderline pattern"; for the rest, "complex mental health problems." The two groups did not differ in how often they chose the lesser verdict of diminished responsibility, which treats mental illness as partly excusing a killing.

claim: Lever pressing dropped faster and more sharply in the rats rewarded for not pressing than in the rats fed regardless.
post: Rats learned to press a lever for food. Then some only got food after a pause with no pressing. Others got food at the same moments no matter what they did. Lever pressing dropped faster and more sharply in the rats rewarded for not pressing than in the rats fed regardless.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: People verified the picture faster and more accurately after the word than after the sound.
post: People heard either a word such as 'cat' or a sound such as a cat meowing, and then saw a picture and said whether it matched. People verified the picture faster and more accurately after the word than after the sound.

claim: Their right-away responses instead resembled the counter-habilitative ones (those that work against a person's growth) found in earlier research on staff.
post: Care staff were asked what they would do, right away and in the long run, about a made-up young man's hard-to-handle behavior. Their long-term plans fit the aims of psychological treatment. Their right-away responses instead resembled the counter-habilitative ones (those that work against a person's growth) found in earlier research on staff.

claim: People given the easy task did better on those problems than the other three groups.
post: People tried to think up unusual uses for objects. Then they had a break with a hard task, an easy task that lets the mind wander, plain rest, or no break, before going back to the same problems. People given the easy task did better on those problems than the other three groups.

claim: One group, who started with moderate distress, improved early, leveled off, then improved again later.
post: People in counseling, mostly at college centers, filled out a well-being questionnaire before every session, for 5 to 25 sessions. Researchers sorted them into three groups by how their scores moved over time. One group, who started with moderate distress, improved early, leveled off, then improved again later.

claim: They recommended the quarterback who saw a sport psychologist less strongly than the one who worked with his coaches.
post: People read a report about a college quarterback who wanted to play more consistently. In one version he worked on it with his coaches, and in the other he worked on it with a sport psychologist. Then people said how strongly they would recommend drafting him. They recommended the quarterback who saw a sport psychologist less strongly than the one who worked with his coaches.
journal: Journal of Sport and Exercise Psychology

claim: The results fit a "low-involvement" pattern, where thinking about a subject and acting on it come before feelings about it.
post: Students in an introductory college chemistry course filled out a questionnaire about how they felt toward chemistry, and their answers were tracked as the course went on. There were no separate groups. The results fit a "low-involvement" pattern, where thinking about a subject and acting on it come before feelings about it.

claim: Students given a combination of representations outperformed students given just one.
post: University students solved logic problems presented in text, in formulas, or in combinations such as text with formulas or text with graphics. Students given a combination of representations outperformed students given just one.

claim: Of the habits measured, being worse at controlling cravings was the strongest sign of eating more high-calorie sweet and savory foods.
post: During a COVID-19 lockdown, people filled out an online survey about how their eating had changed and about their eating habits, including how well they could resist cravings. Of the habits measured, being worse at controlling cravings was the strongest sign of eating more high-calorie sweet and savory foods.

claim: Students who said they study by choice got better grades only if the word task also showed it and their working memory was average or high.
post: College students filled out a questionnaire on how much they study by choice, did a word task meant to detect that motivation without asking, and took memory tests. Grades were collected at semester's end. Students who said they study by choice got better grades only if the word task also showed it and their working memory was average or high.

claim: After the germ pictures, people's picks changed mainly for opposite-sex faces, not same-sex faces.
post: People picked the more attractive face from pairs, such as a more masculine and a more feminine version of one face. Then some watched pictures hinting at germs, while others saw pictures with no such cues, and everyone picked again. After the germ pictures, people's picks changed mainly for opposite-sex faces, not same-sex faces.

claim: Each kind of brain measure predicted improvement better than starting severity did.
post: People with social anxiety had their brains scanned while resting, then took a course of cognitive behavioral therapy, a type of talk therapy. Their improvement was predicted either from the brain scans or from how severe their anxiety was at the start. Each kind of brain measure predicted improvement better than starting severity did.

claim: The answers sorted into seven kinds of playfulness, such as cheerful, whimsical and impulsive, and the two questionnaires left some of them out.
post: People read statements that describe playful adults, which the researchers built from an analysis of everyday language. They also filled out two existing playfulness questionnaires. The answers sorted into seven kinds of playfulness, such as cheerful, whimsical and impulsive, and the two questionnaires left some of them out.

claim: A month later, the first group had fewer trauma symptoms than the second, counting where each person started.
post: People who had lived through a traumatic event and were very afraid of feeling anxious were split into two groups. One group got a program meant to lower that fear. The other got a comparison program. A month later, the first group had fewer trauma symptoms than the second, counting where each person started.

claim: People who usually get less enjoyment from things rated that relief as less pleasant.
post: People learned that some symbols meant an upsetting picture might appear, and others meant it was safe. Then, when a symbol signaled a threat, they could take an action to stop the picture from showing. After each time the picture was successfully stopped, they rated how pleasant the relief felt. People who usually get less enjoyment from things rated that relief as less pleasant.

claim: Students in the skills program reported more exercise and sport than those in regular gym.
post: Some high school classes had regular gym lessons for 7 weeks. Other classes got a short skills program built into gym, with four 20-minute lessons and two times to reflect. Students reported how much they exercised and played sports. Students in the skills program reported more exercise and sport than those in regular gym.

claim: The more lopsided a person's face was, the less attractive their voice was rated, in both men and women.
post: College students read the first sentences of a passage aloud into a microphone, and each had a front-facing photo taken with a neutral expression. Strangers of the opposite sex rated how attractive each voice was. The more lopsided a person's face was, the less attractive their voice was rated, in both men and women.

claim: Early security predicted adult security only in people with the G/G version of an oxytocin receptor gene, not those with other versions.
post: Babies stayed in a lab while their mothers left and came back, and were rated on how secure they seemed. Years later they were interviewed about their parents and partners, and gave cheek cell samples. Early security predicted adult security only in people with the G/G version of an oxytocin receptor gene, not those with other versions.
journal: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry

claim: The group with psychosis reported less satisfaction of these basic needs.
post: People who had recently had their first episode of psychosis filled out a 21-item questionnaire about their lives. It asked how much they felt in control of their choices, capable, and connected to others. People without psychosis of the same age also answered it. The group with psychosis reported less satisfaction of these basic needs.

claim: Guilt was the best predictor of these thoughts and urges, while depression and anxiety were not strong predictors.
post: College students ticked off the unwanted thoughts and urges that had popped into their heads on a checklist. They also filled out questionnaires on how depressed, anxious, and guilty they felt. Guilt was the best predictor of these thoughts and urges, while depression and anxiety were not strong predictors.

claim: Both kinds of training led to gains in how fluently the children read words.
post: Children with dyslexia did 8 weeks of training on reading words by sounding them out, and 8 weeks of training on learning tricky words as whole shapes. Some did sounding out first, some did whole words first, and some did both together. Both kinds of training led to gains in how fluently the children read words.

claim: Ethnicity was used more over time, but in 1995 to 1998 three quarters of articles still left it out.
post: A team went through articles on child abuse and neglect from three journals, published between 1977 and 1998. They checked whether each article reported participants' ethnicity and whether it used ethnicity in its analysis or design. Ethnicity was used more over time, but in 1995 to 1998 three quarters of articles still left it out.

claim: With either hormone, they moved their money toward riskier investments than they did with the dummy.
post: Young men came to a lab twice, at least a week apart. One time they took a stress hormone (cortisol) or a male sex hormone (testosterone), and the other time a dummy treatment, without knowing which. Then they played a trading game with investments. With either hormone, they moved their money toward riskier investments than they did with the dummy.

claim: The higher people scored on neuroticism, a lasting tendency toward anxiety and negative feelings, the bigger their twitch to the pair compared with the strong pulse alone.
post: People took a personality test, then got magnetic pulses to the head that made a muscle twitch. Sometimes a weak pulse came just before a strong one. The higher people scored on neuroticism, a lasting tendency toward anxiety and negative feelings, the bigger their twitch to the pair compared with the strong pulse alone.

claim: The first item's good or bad feeling still affected how people named the second one, even without repetition.
post: People saw one item flash up, then a second item that they had to name out loud. The first item felt either pleasant or unpleasant. In some versions the items were shown again and again, and in others no item was ever repeated. The first item's good or bad feeling still affected how people named the second one, even without repetition.

claim: Among the guarded patients, the two were unrelated.
post: Patients hoping to get on a heart transplant list took a personality questionnaire about their emotional distress, plus a set of thinking tests. Some answered the questionnaire in a guarded way, trying to look good, and others did not. Among the open patients, more distress went with worse thinking scores. Among the guarded patients, the two were unrelated.

claim: Children who thought other children had eaten a large amount of carrots ate more carrots than all the others.
post: Children aged 6 to 11 were told about the carrots other children had eaten: a large amount, none, or no information. Then they got carrots to eat. Children who thought other children had eaten a large amount of carrots ate more carrots than all the others.
journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity

claim: People's answers shifted toward what the other person said more for neutral pictures than for emotional ones.
post: People looked at pictures that were positive, negative or neutral. Then they said which pictures they had seen before, mixed in with new ones. Another person, who was working with the researchers, gave wrong answers, correct answers or none. People's answers shifted toward what the other person said more for neutral pictures than for emotional ones.

claim: The students who did the tasks understood more of the new words and plural forms than the class that only took the tests.
post: Beginner French students at a state school spent two lessons doing tasks that got them to notice how French shows plurals, and the teacher never explained the rule. A comparison class only took the tests. The students who did the tasks understood more of the new words and plural forms than the class that only took the tests.

claim: Even when people did not notice a change, they still showed sensitivity to it.
post: People did visual tasks in which something in a scene changes, which people often fail to notice. The researchers modified these tasks. Even when people did not notice a change, they still showed sensitivity to it.

claim: People without depression changed their guesses more when the news was better than expected than when it was worse, but people with depression did not show this pattern.
post: People guessed their own chances of going through 70 bad life events, like a robbery or Alzheimer's disease. After each guess they were shown the average person's real chances, then guessed again. Some were people with depression and some were not. People without depression changed their guesses more when the news was better than expected than when it was worse, but people with depression did not show this pattern.

claim: Those scores were linked to both how well the salespeople performed and how much sales experience they had.
post: Salespeople from many kinds of companies filled out a questionnaire they got in the mail about how they listen to customers. Each person's answers were turned into a listening score. Those scores were linked to both how well the salespeople performed and how much sales experience they had.
journal: Journal of Marketing Theory and Practice

claim: Once that gap was accounted for, the girl-boy difference in plans for math fields shrank by around 75%.
post: Students in 64 countries were tested in reading and math and asked if they planned to study or work in math-heavy fields. Girls were stronger in reading compared with math than boys were. Once that gap was accounted for, the girl-boy difference in plans for math fields shrank by around 75%.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: Readers rated the couples as feeling better when they had talked about their relationship.
post: Married people read short stories about couples having pleasant or unpleasant moments. In some stories the couple talked about their relationship, and in others they did not. After each story, readers rated how content the characters felt. Readers rated the couples as feeling better when they had talked about their relationship.
journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships

claim: Emotional abuse was the main predictor of having more symptoms, over and above the other kinds of abuse and neglect.
post: Young people at high risk were asked about abuse and neglect in their past, and about their mental health: emotional troubles, behavior problems, and trauma symptoms. Some had lived through several kinds of mistreatment, others fewer. Emotional abuse was the main predictor of having more symptoms, over and above the other kinds of abuse and neglect.

claim: People with OCD had a larger attention-related brain signal, which came sooner on the right side, and reacted faster to target tones.
post: People listened to tones, including target tones they had to react to, while their brain activity was recorded. Some had OCD and took no medication. Others were healthy and matched for age and sex. People with OCD had a larger attention-related brain signal, which came sooner on the right side, and reacted faster to target tones.

claim: The game cut down the out-of-seat and talking-out behavior, first in math period and then in reading period.
post: A fourth-grade class was split into two teams to play a game. Each time a child left their seat or talked out of turn, a mark went on the chalkboard, and everyone on that team could lose privileges like extra recess. The game cut down the out-of-seat and talking-out behavior, first in math period and then in reading period.

claim: The symptoms split into two separate sets: one for grief, such as yearning and disbelief about the death, and one for depression.
post: Older people whose husband or wife had died a few months earlier answered questions about how they were feeling. Researchers then checked which symptoms tended to show up together. The symptoms split into two separate sets: one for grief, such as yearning and disbelief about the death, and one for depression.

claim: People who left others more choice scored higher on honesty, agreeableness, empathy, and caring about others' outcomes.
post: People made choices where they could leave another person with more options or fewer options. They also filled out questionnaires about their personality, their empathy, and how much they care about good outcomes for others. People who left others more choice scored higher on honesty, agreeableness, empathy, and caring about others' outcomes.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Over the training, the scores changed for both the mother's behavior and the girl's.
post: A mother gave her 3-year-old daughter set commands, like "Put the book on the table," while an observer scored how each of them acted. The girl had a diagnosis for defiant behavior, and the mother was in parent training. Over the training, the scores changed for both the mother's behavior and the girl's.

claim: This was strongest in Americans, in the middle for the British and Germans, and absent in Japanese students.
post: College students in the US, Britain, Germany and Japan did tasks meant to show how much people see themselves as separate from others. One measure looked for a puffed-up sense of self. This was strongest in Americans, in the middle for the British and Germans, and absent in Japanese students.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: A single brief mismatch on one trial was enough to shift what people judged as simultaneous on the next trial.
post: People watched a ring flash on a screen while a short beep played through headphones. Sometimes the beep came just before the ring, sometimes just after, and sometimes together. After each one they said whether the two happened at the same time. A single brief mismatch on one trial was enough to shift what people judged as simultaneous on the next trial.

claim: People who felt grateful put in more effort to help than people who did not feel grateful.
post: Some people were made to feel grateful to another person, and others were made to feel good in general. Then everyone could help that person, even though helping was unpleasant. People who felt grateful put in more effort to help than people who did not feel grateful.

claim: Students with more self-control had weaker unhealthy-snacking habits, and those weaker habits accounted for why they ate fewer unhealthy snacks.
post: Students who said they were trying to eat healthily answered questions about self-control and how automatically they ate unhealthy snacks. Then they kept a diary of their snacks for a week. Students with more self-control had weaker unhealthy-snacking habits, and those weaker habits accounted for why they ate fewer unhealthy snacks.

claim: Snacks from the kind each person liked best, including ones not in the choosing game, worked as rewards for them.
post: Six people with developmental disabilities were shown snack items two at a time and picked the one they wanted. The snacks came from four kinds: chocolate, salty and crunchy, gummy, and fruit and vegetable. Snacks from the kind each person liked best, including ones not in the choosing game, worked as rewards for them.

claim: In both, the answers fit the chain the researchers expected: needs met, then self-driven motivation, then plans, then behavior.
post: University students filled out surveys on how well their basic needs were met, why they exercise or diet, what they planned to do, and what they did. The surveys covered two areas: exercise and dieting. In both, the answers fit the chain the researchers expected: needs met, then self-driven motivation, then plans, then behavior.

claim: Counselors who ran into more ethical dilemmas reported more burnout and stress.
post: Practicing counselors reported how often they ran into ethical dilemmas at work, how often they reflected on them, and how burned out and stressed they felt. Counselors who ran into more ethical dilemmas reported more burnout and stress.

claim: The step-by-step clips helped almost everyone learn quickly, but the single long video mostly did not help.
post: Six adults with developmental disabilities learned to set a table and put away groceries by watching videos. For some tasks, they watched 10 short clips, each showing one step, and then tried the task. For others, they watched one long video showing all 10 steps. The step-by-step clips helped almost everyone learn quickly, but the single long video mostly did not help.
journal: Education and Training in Developmental Disabilities

claim: Students who felt more nervous talking with others scored lower on the video task.
post: College students filled out questionnaires about how nervous they feel when talking with others and how shy or sociable they are. They also watched a set of short videotaped scenes of people interacting and answered questions about what was going on between them. Students who felt more nervous talking with others scored lower on the video task.

claim: Being told made truth tellers, but not liars, give more details that could be checked.
post: People wrote statements about an event, some as mock criminals who were lying and some as innocent people telling the truth. Half of each group were told beforehand that their statements would be checked for details that could be verified. Being told made truth tellers, but not liars, give more details that could be checked.

claim: The players whose drive came most from inside themselves were more likely to make the national team than the other players.
post: Ninety-seven top young football players answered questions about what drives them: why they play, what goals they set, and how much they want to achieve. A year later, the researchers checked which players had made the under-15 national team. The players whose drive came most from inside themselves were more likely to make the national team than the other players.

claim: People primed to focus on differences were more likely to do so than people who were not.
post: Some people were first led to think about the ways they differ from other people. Then they were tested on whether they would take another person's visual point of view without being asked. People primed to focus on differences were more likely to do so than people who were not.

claim: The students who got the real pulses reported about 33% less belief in positive religious ideas, such as God, angels and Heaven, than the fake-pulse group.
post: College students wrote about their own death. Some had first received magnetic pulses to a spot in the front of the brain, and others got a fake version. Then everyone rated statements like "There exists an all-powerful, all-knowing, loving God." The students who got the real pulses reported about 33% less belief in positive religious ideas, such as God, angels and Heaven, than the fake-pulse group.

claim: Men's and women's personality profiles overlapped by only about 10%, a very large overall difference.
post: Women and men across the US filled out a personality questionnaire covering 15 traits, such as warmth, dominance and tension. The researchers combined the differences on all 15 traits into one overall score. Men's and women's personality profiles overlapped by only about 10%, a very large overall difference.

claim: Students recognized the women and the people of color less than the White men.
post: Junior and senior psychology majors saw a list of 42 famous names in psychology, half men and half women, including several people of color. For each name, they rated how well they knew the person, from never heard of them to could describe most of their work. Students recognized the women and the people of color less than the White men.
journal: Psi Chi Journal of Psychological Research

claim: Among depressed patients, naming the color took longer when both words described them than when only the second one did.
post: Depressed patients, anxious patients and people with neither problem saw a word, then a second word printed in color, and named the color. Some words were adjectives they had rated as describing themselves. Among depressed patients, naming the color took longer when both words described them than when only the second one did.

claim: Students who wrote about overweight characters wrote sadder, more negative stories and made the characters more unpleasant than students who wrote about normal-weight characters.
post: College students wrote short stories about a man or a woman. Some saw a picture or a written description of an overweight character, and others saw a normal-weight character. Students who wrote about overweight characters wrote sadder, more negative stories and made the characters more unpleasant than students who wrote about normal-weight characters.

claim: Memories about academic stress were far more common among the Chinese students (28 of 120) than the American students (4 of 120).
post: College students in China and in the US each wrote down two memories that said the most about who they are. Researchers sorted the memories into types, such as achievement or guilt and shame. Memories about academic stress were far more common among the Chinese students (28 of 120) than the American students (4 of 120).

claim: Husbands who rated themselves as more emotionally mature tended to score higher on how well their marriage was working.
post: Married couples each filled out a questionnaire about how emotionally mature they were and another about how well their marriage was working. Each spouse also rated the other's maturity in private. Husbands who rated themselves as more emotionally mature tended to score higher on how well their marriage was working.
journal: Journal of Marriage and the Family

claim: Healthy people adapted to clashes from one trial to the next, but people with the disorder were completely unable to.
post: People in a brain scanner judged whether faces looked happy or fearful, with the word "HAPPY" or "FEAR" written across each face, sometimes clashing. Some people had generalized anxiety disorder; others did not. Healthy people adapted to clashes from one trial to the next, but people with the disorder were completely unable to.

claim: People without neuroscience training rated explanations as more satisfying when they included the brain information.
post: People read short descriptions of psychological findings, each followed by an explanation of why it happens. Some explanations were good and some just restated the finding. Half the people saw explanations with an added, irrelevant line about brain scans, and half saw none. People without neuroscience training rated explanations as more satisfying when they included the brain information.

claim: Older adults did worse than younger adults without the closeness, but with it they did about as well as younger adults.
post: Younger and older adults took tests of spotting awkward remarks and reading other people's emotions. Some were made to feel close to the experimenter or the person in the task, and others were not. Older adults did worse than younger adults without the closeness, but with it they did about as well as younger adults.

claim: People who disliked uncertainty more tended to pick the quick, smaller, less likely prize.
post: People played a gambling game where each round offered a choice. They could take a small prize right away that was unlikely to pay off, or wait a bit for a bigger prize that was more likely to pay off. They also rated how much they dislike not knowing what will happen. People who disliked uncertainty more tended to pick the quick, smaller, less likely prize.

claim: The honest students gave longer, more detailed answers and admitted more possible mistakes than the liars.
post: College students went into a professor's office and either stole an exam or put back an exam that had been stolen earlier. A week later, each was interviewed. Half told the truth and half lied to avoid blame. The honest students gave longer, more detailed answers and admitted more possible mistakes than the liars.
journal: Journal of Investigative Psychology and Offender Profiling

claim: Among people who don't, it was the reverse.
post: People got bursts of mildly painful heat and rated them. Some heard a recording guiding them to pay attention to their breathing and body sensations, and others heard fairy tales. Among people who tend to think the worst about pain, the guided group felt less pain than the story group. Among people who don't, it was the reverse.

claim: Children in the matched-plan schools improved more on sounding out words and reading aloud smoothly.
post: First graders who were struggling to read got extra small-group help every day, in schools assigned by chance to one of two plans. In some schools, regular class reading lessons were improved and the extra help matched them. Others used the standard district lessons and help. Children in the matched-plan schools improved more on sounding out words and reading aloud smoothly.

claim: Babies with both risk variations had about ten times the odds of disorganized attachment, meaning confused, mixed-up behavior toward the caregiver.
post: Babies went through a mildly stressful lab visit where they were briefly separated from their caregiver, and researchers watched how they acted. Their DNA was checked for two variations in one gene. Babies with both risk variations had about ten times the odds of disorganized attachment, meaning confused, mixed-up behavior toward the caregiver.

claim: Those given positive ideas tended to do better on memory, while those given negative ideas tended to do worse.
post: Older adults went through a session that quietly brought to mind either positive or negative ideas about aging, without them realizing it. Then their memory was tested. Those given positive ideas tended to do better on memory, while those given negative ideas tended to do worse.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: The more multilingual people were, the more easily they said they adjusted their goals.
post: Adults filled out an online questionnaire about the languages they speak, how well they know each one, and how much they use it. They also rated statements like "I can adapt quite easily to changes in a situation." The more multilingual people were, the more easily they said they adjusted their goals.
journal: Journal of Multilingual and Multicultural Development

claim: The study suggested that how the women reacted to their parents' behavior may matter more than the parents' behavior alone.
post: Women who were lesbian and women who were straight, none of them in clinical care, filled out a questionnaire about their relationships with their parents. The study suggested that how the women reacted to their parents' behavior may matter more than the parents' behavior alone.

claim: Voter turnout rose substantially with canvassing, slightly with mail, and not at all with phone calls.
post: In New Haven, registered voters were randomly assigned to receive a get-out-the-vote message just before an election, from a canvasser in person, by mail, or by telephone. Then researchers checked who voted. Voter turnout rose substantially with canvassing, slightly with mail, and not at all with phone calls.

claim: Thirteen of 17 students passed every matching and spoken test.
post: College students were taught to name a set of visual items, then taught to answer one spoken word with a related word. Afterward they matched the items to each other and answered spoken tests, including with new sets. In a second experiment, some of the matching tests were left out. Thirteen of 17 students passed every matching and spoken test.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: The children did not learn to play cooperatively until the out-loud description was added to the training.
post: Six children with autism watched two models act out a play scene together, then stepped into one model's role while the same scene was repeated. For some training rounds, the children also had to describe the scene out loud before they joined in. The children did not learn to play cooperatively until the out-loud description was added to the training.

claim: Among students who replayed worries a lot, the more mindful ones were less likely to feel they couldn't stop.
post: Students were measured on how mindful they naturally are, meaning how well they stay in the present moment. They were also measured on how much they replay worries in their heads and how out of control that replaying felt. Among students who replayed worries a lot, the more mindful ones were less likely to feel they couldn't stop.

claim: Men who tend to worry about being close to others rated themselves as less independent and self-confident after oxytocin than after the placebo, while the average man showed no change.
post: Men got a nasal spray with oxytocin, a hormone linked to bonding, on one visit and a spray with no active ingredient on another. Afterward they rated themselves on traits like "independent" and "self-confident." Men who tend to worry about being close to others rated themselves as less independent and self-confident after oxytocin than after the placebo, while the average man showed no change.

claim: Their own ratings of growth were generally unrelated to how much their answers actually changed.
post: Students filled out questionnaires about things like how they relate to others and how they see life. Two months later they did it again. Some had a traumatic event in between and also rated how much they had grown from it. Their own ratings of growth were generally unrelated to how much their answers actually changed.

claim: Among kids with a disorganized bond to their mother, those high on both defiance and little guilt were likelier to stay highly aggressive: 38% versus 7% overall.
post: Mothers rated their 3-year-olds on defiance, tantrums and showing little guilt. The children also took part in a lab session with their mother that measured their bond, and teachers rated their aggression each year through sixth grade. Among kids with a disorganized bond to their mother, those high on both defiance and little guilt were likelier to stay highly aggressive: 38% versus 7% overall.
journal: Journal of Psychopathology and Behavioral Assessment

claim: All three groups binged less over time, with no difference among them, and all did better than the waiting list.
post: Women with binge eating problems joined group sessions for 8 weeks. Some had a therapist lead everything, some watched a taped lesson and then talked with a therapist, and some watched the tape and led their own talk. Others were put on a waiting list. All three groups binged less over time, with no difference among them, and all did better than the waiting list.

claim: They fell into two clusters: people who matched the rhythm and people who did not.
post: People listened to a steady stream of random syllables played at a fixed pace, while whispering syllables of their own at the same time. Researchers measured how closely each person's whispering lined up with the beat they heard. The scores did not spread evenly. They fell into two clusters: people who matched the rhythm and people who did not.

claim: The more binge eating problems a group had, the more dieting, impulsivity, and perfectionism they showed, and the lower their self-esteem.
post: Obese women answered a structured interview about their eating before starting a weight-loss program. Based on it, they were sorted into four groups: no overeating, overeating without feeling out of control, overeating with loss of control, and full binge eating disorder. The more binge eating problems a group had, the more dieting, impulsivity, and perfectionism they showed, and the lower their self-esteem.

claim: Women gave more correct answers than men.
post: College students got pairs of signals and said whether the two were the same or different. A pair could be two sounds, two visual signals, or one of each in either order. Women gave more correct answers than men.

claim: Both men and women rated the photos taken in the fertile window as more attractive than the photos taken in the later phase.
post: Women were photographed at two points in their menstrual cycle: during the days when they could most easily get pregnant, and during a later phase of the cycle. Men and women then looked at the photos and rated how attractive each face was. Both men and women rated the photos taken in the fertile window as more attractive than the photos taken in the later phase.
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series B: Biological Sciences

claim: The people who chewed gum reported feeling less stressed, both at work and in life in general, than the people who didn't.
post: Full-time workers filled out an online survey about how often they chewed gum, how stressed they felt at work and in life, and their health. About six in ten were gum chewers. The people who chewed gum reported feeling less stressed, both at work and in life in general, than the people who didn't.

claim: Conservatives who saw McCain as more a part of themselves felt those needs were met less than conservatives who saw him as less a part of themselves.
post: After John McCain lost the 2008 U.S. presidential election, conservative voters rated how much they saw him as part of themselves. They also rated how much they felt they belonged, felt good about themselves, felt in control, and felt life had meaning. Conservatives who saw McCain as more a part of themselves felt those needs were met less than conservatives who saw him as less a part of themselves.
journal: Analyses of Social Issues and Public Policy

claim: Those who tend to hold back when things are uncertain had a smaller one.
post: People answered questions about how much uncertainty bothers them. Then they did a computer task that makes mistakes likely, while their brain activity was recorded. Those more distressed by uncertainty had a bigger brain response to mistakes. Those who tend to hold back when things are uncertain had a smaller one.

claim: People who were asked about one person first gave more to the group.
post: Some people were first asked how much they would donate to help one needy person, and then how much to donate to help a whole group of needy people. Others were asked only about the group. People who were asked about one person first gave more to the group.

claim: People who had thought about death accepted a smaller later reward in place of the $50 than people who had thought about dental pain.
post: People thought about their own death or about dental pain. Then they chose between $50 now and increasingly attractive rewards in three months. People who had thought about death accepted a smaller later reward in place of the $50 than people who had thought about dental pain.

claim: After the "Mommy and I are one" message, the women gave fewer depression-related responses.
post: Women being treated for depression were shown messages flashed too fast to notice consciously. One message read "Mommy and I are one." Other messages, like "Succeed for myself," were tested too. After the "Mommy and I are one" message, the women gave fewer depression-related responses.
journal: Journal of the American Academy of Psychoanalysis

claim: Students whose gambling put them at higher risk scored lower on self-control than students at lower risk.
post: College students filled out a questionnaire about how well they control their impulses and emotions. They also answered questions about their gambling, such as whether they had bet more than they could afford to lose. Students whose gambling put them at higher risk scored lower on self-control than students at lower risk.

claim: The more childhood trauma a woman had been through, the more likely she was to drop out of treatment.
post: Researchers went back through the clinic files of 111 women who had come for treatment of bulimia, an eating disorder. They checked which women had quit therapy early and what had happened to them in childhood. The more childhood trauma a woman had been through, the more likely she was to drop out of treatment.

claim: Words with many look-alikes were named faster than words with few, but not when their letters were easily confused.
post: A patient who reads one letter at a time named written words out loud. Some words had many look-alikes that differ by one letter, others few, and some had easily confused letters. Words with many look-alikes were named faster than words with few, but not when their letters were easily confused.

claim: Most children improved by a large amount in the first month, and kept improving through month four.
post: Teachers of children with attention or behavior problems used a daily report card, a regular rating of how the child did on set behavior goals. Each teacher got coaching from a clinician, counselor, or social worker. Behavior was tracked month by month. Most children improved by a large amount in the first month, and kept improving through month four.

claim: The reading fluency and comprehension of students with reading disabilities improved more with this than without it.
post: Elementary school students were randomly put into two groups. One group heard a positive label, like "clever," tied to a specific reading habit, such as answering questions. They were also challenged to do better than before and better than another student. The reading fluency and comprehension of students with reading disabilities improved more with this than without it.

claim: Households that heard the pennies price plus the bargain line were more likely to buy than households that got the usual dollar price.
post: People going door to door sold packs of note cards to raise money for a local charity. Some sellers gave the price in dollars. Others said it in pennies, "300 pennies," and then right away added "It's a bargain." Households that heard the pennies price plus the bargain line were more likely to buy than households that got the usual dollar price.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Even clips rated as heavily accented were mostly understood, so a strong accent did not necessarily make speech harder to understand.
post: People listened to short clips of spontaneous English speech from Mandarin speakers and two native English speakers. They typed what they heard and rated how foreign each accent sounded and how easy it was to understand. Even clips rated as heavily accented were mostly understood, so a strong accent did not necessarily make speech harder to understand.

claim: The bowing portraits got higher attractiveness ratings than the other two kinds.
post: People saw face portraits from university yearbooks on a computer screen and rated how attractive each face was, from 0 to 100. Some portraits were tilted toward the viewer, like a greeting bow. Others tilted backward or stayed still. The bowing portraits got higher attractiveness ratings than the other two kinds.

claim: The AI answers were rated as more creative on average than the answers from the people.
post: People and three AI chatbots were each given four everyday objects, such as a rope or a candle. Everyone was asked for creative, unusual uses for each one, in 1 to 3 words. The AI answers were rated as more creative on average than the answers from the people.

claim: Both groups applied the name more narrowly, only to objects most like the named ones, when the teacher chose than when they chose themselves.
post: Children and adults learned names for new kinds of objects. In one version, a knowledgeable teacher chose which objects got named. In the other, the learners chose them. Both groups applied the name more narrowly, only to objects most like the named ones, when the teacher chose than when they chose themselves.

claim: People were slower to name the color when the word clashed with it than when it matched.
post: People were timed naming the ink colors of words like "hot" and "cold" printed on cards. On some cards, the feel of the word matched the feel of the color. On others, it clashed. People were slower to name the color when the word clashed with it than when it matched.

claim: Wives' sense of body space changed over that time, but husbands' did not, so spouses' patterns did not match.
post: Married couples were followed from the third month of pregnancy to two months after the birth. Wives and husbands each reported how much space they felt their own bodies took up. Wives' sense of body space changed over that time, but husbands' did not, so spouses' patterns did not match.

claim: Among patients expected to do badly in treatment, those whose therapists got feedback had better outcomes than those whose therapists did not.
post: Patients went through psychotherapy while their progress was tracked. For some patients, their therapists were given feedback on how the patient was doing. For others, therapists got no feedback. Among patients expected to do badly in treatment, those whose therapists got feedback had better outcomes than those whose therapists did not.

claim: The estimates tracked the long test's scores closely (correlations of .87 and .85) and did not run too high.
post: Psychiatric patients in a veterans hospital took a short test and a long standard IQ test. Researchers built a formula that turns short-test scores into an estimated IQ, using 100 patients, then tried it on 50 new patients. The estimates tracked the long test's scores closely (correlations of .87 and .85) and did not run too high.

claim: Anxiety went down about equally for the mandala and plaid colorers, and more than for the blank-paper colorers.
post: Students first did a brief task that made them anxious. Then some colored a mandala, some colored a plaid pattern, and some colored on a blank piece of paper. Anxiety went down about equally for the mandala and plaid colorers, and more than for the blank-paper colorers.

claim: The machine players went from regular gambling to a gambling problem in about 1 year, compared with about 3.6 years for the others.
post: People seeking treatment for a gambling problem filled out a questionnaire about their gambling history and answered a doctor's interview. Some had mainly played gambling machines, and others had mainly played older kinds of gambling. The machine players went from regular gambling to a gambling problem in about 1 year, compared with about 3.6 years for the others.

claim: Students who saw the high-credibility video came away with higher self-esteem than the others.
post: College students who scored low on a self-esteem test were split into three groups. Two groups watched a video with a message against their low opinion of themselves, one told as coming from a highly credible source and one from a less credible source. The third group watched nothing. Students who saw the high-credibility video came away with higher self-esteem than the others.

claim: People with heart failure were worse at remembering than the comparison group, across these task types.
post: People with chronic heart failure and people without it did a lab task that imitates remembering to do things later in a normal day. Some tasks were cued by an event, some by a time, and some repeated. People with heart failure were worse at remembering than the comparison group, across these task types.
journal: Journal of the International Neuropsychological Society

claim: The held boys generally scored lower, and the authors concluded the non-delinquent scores were not a fair yardstick for them.
post: Boys being held while they waited for court hearings looked at inkblots and described what they saw. Their answers were scored, then compared with scores from teenage boys who were not delinquent. The held boys generally scored lower, and the authors concluded the non-delinquent scores were not a fair yardstick for them.
journal: Journal of Projective Techniques & Personality Assessment

claim: They also did worse than native speakers at basic processing of the wording.
post: Native English speakers and people who speak English very well as a second language were tested on how well they understood the Miranda rights, the warnings read to suspects in the US.
