post: Staff at a national education service in New Zealand were trained to assess children's behavior and write support plans. Some were trained by outside experts, and others by the service's own newly trained team. Their work was checked against 140 set criteria. The in-house team trained staff to meet the same standards as the outside experts.

claim: The weapon's effect on memory was weaker when the man was Black than when he was White.
post: White and Black people acted as eyewitnesses to a man who either held a weapon or did not. For some people the man was White, and for others he was Black. Later their memory of him was tested. The weapon's effect on memory was weaker when the man was Black than when he was White.

claim: Accuracy was low with the first, but the teachers carried out the tests accurately with the improved instructions.
post: Teachers who had never run a preference test practiced offering snacks to a pretend client to see which one the client picked. They first used written instructions alone, then a version with less jargon plus pictures, diagrams, and step-by-step examples. Accuracy was low with the first, but the teachers carried out the tests accurately with the improved instructions.

claim: Responses were affected both by whether the ignored words matched the middle word and by whether they shared its key, a link made only by the instructions.
post: People saw three color words stacked on a screen and pressed a left or right key for the middle word, ignoring the other two. Each key stood for two of the four words. Responses were affected both by whether the ignored words matched the middle word and by whether they shared its key, a link made only by the instructions.

claim: For users, more worry went with a bigger brain response to mistakes; for nonusers the link was smaller and unclear.
post: Women wore a cap recording brain activity while pressing keys for the middle letter in a row of letters, then rated their worry. Some used hormonal birth control and some did not. For users, more worry went with a bigger brain response to mistakes; for nonusers the link was smaller and unclear.

claim: The older the person being rated, the more negative the ratings were.
post: College students rated imaginary people on a set of opposite-word scales, such as good versus bad. Some rated 25-year-olds, some 50-year-olds, and some 75-year-olds, and the people being rated were either men or women. The older the person being rated, the more negative the ratings were.

claim: The men who got testosterone scored lower than the men who got the placebo.
post: Men were given either a single dose of testosterone or a placebo. Then they answered brain teasers where the first answer that comes to mind is wrong and you have to stop and think. The men who got testosterone scored lower than the men who got the placebo.

claim: Sound in the left ear disrupted people more than sound in the right, but only when the ignored sound changed in an ordered way and the task meant keeping things in order.
post: People did mental tasks while sounds they were told to ignore played in their left ear or their right ear. In some versions the ignored sound changed more, in others less. Sound in the left ear disrupted people more than sound in the right, but only when the ignored sound changed in an ordered way and the task meant keeping things in order.

claim: When people lied, four brain areas were more active than when they told the truth.
post: People lay in a brain scanner and played a money game with a partner they never met. They saw how much money each of two options (Blue or Red) would pay, then told the partner which option was better for the partner. They could lie or tell the truth. When people lied, four brain areas were more active than when they told the truth.

claim: Her anxious thoughts about pain declined, even though the treatment never targeted them directly.
post: One woman who had lived with chronic pain for 11 years went through a treatment that taught her to relax, scheduled activities she valued, and showed her graphs of her progress. Her worries about pain were measured before and after. Her anxious thoughts about pain declined, even though the treatment never targeted them directly.
journal: International Journal of Behavioral Consultation and Therapy

claim: People who got adjectives focused more on the big picture, while people who got verbs focused more on the details.
post: People used or saw words that were either adjectives, which are abstract, or verbs, which are more concrete. Then they did tasks that showed whether they focused on the big picture or on the details. People who got adjectives focused more on the big picture, while people who got verbs focused more on the details.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Men in the romantic mindset no longer weighed losses more heavily than gains, which people usually do.
post: Some men and women were put in a mindset about finding a romantic partner, and others in a mindset about protecting themselves from danger. Then they made choices involving possible gains and losses. Men in the romantic mindset no longer weighed losses more heavily than gains, which people usually do.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: After bigger drops in how much of the session it was available, the destructive behavior came back more than after smaller drops.
post: People in a clinic were treated for destructive behavior by getting what they wanted when they asked in a better way. Step by step, that payoff was made available for less of each session. After bigger drops in how much of the session it was available, the destructive behavior came back more than after smaller drops.
journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior

claim: People who used the slur for themselves felt more powerful, and observers saw them and their group as more powerful.
post: In some cases, people called themselves by a slur that others use against their group, such as "queer" or "bitch." In other cases, they used a plain label like "woman." People who used the slur for themselves felt more powerful, and observers saw them and their group as more powerful.

claim: Their Ouija board answers were right about 65% of the time.
post: People answered yes/no questions in two ways: by saying the answer out loud, and by resting their hands on a Ouija board and letting it move. When they felt they were only guessing, their spoken answers were right half the time, which is chance. Their Ouija board answers were right about 65% of the time.

claim: Patients who felt more criticized before treatment had more severe anxiety after treatment, beyond what their symptoms before treatment would predict.
post: Patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder or panic disorder with agoraphobia rated how much criticism they felt from family members, and their anxiety symptoms were measured. Then they went through behavioral treatment, and symptoms were measured again. Patients who felt more criticized before treatment had more severe anxiety after treatment, beyond what their symptoms before treatment would predict.

claim: Rhyming pairs got quicker answers than unrelated pairs, and the speedup was equal whether or not the spellings matched.
post: People saw two strings of letters, one after the other, and pressed a button to say whether each was a real word. Some pairs rhymed and looked alike (BRIBE-TRIBE), some rhymed but were spelled differently (EIGHT-MATE), and some were unrelated. Rhyming pairs got quicker answers than unrelated pairs, and the speedup was equal whether or not the spellings matched.

claim: Neuroticism scores were not reliably linked to the number of copies, though they tended to rise with more copies.
post: Adults filled out a questionnaire measuring neuroticism, the tendency to feel negative emotions. Their DNA was checked at one spot in a gene called MAMDC1, where people carry zero, one, or two copies of a less common version. Neuroticism scores were not reliably linked to the number of copies, though they tended to rise with more copies.

claim: Oxytocin improved accuracy only for the less socially skilled people.
post: People sniffed a nasal spray with oxytocin, a hormone, on one occasion and a spray with no drug on another. Each time they did a task testing how accurately they read other people's feelings, and they also filled out a questionnaire on social skills. Oxytocin improved accuracy only for the less socially skilled people.

claim: Coaching increased how closely they followed the method's steps.
post: Six graduate students training to be special education teachers practiced in a simulated classroom while a coach worked with them one-on-one. They were learning a method for teaching students with autism: give the smallest hint first, and add more help only if needed. Coaching increased how closely they followed the method's steps.
journal: Teacher Education and Special Education: The Journal of the Teacher Education Division of the Council for Exceptional Children

claim: They linked "and" with disks that changed together, and "or" with disks that took turns.
post: People watched two colored disks disappear and reappear on a screen, with a phrase like "the purple and the green" or "the purple or the green" above them. The disks either vanished together or took turns. People judged whether the phrase matched. They linked "and" with disks that changed together, and "or" with disks that took turns.

claim: People who turned the crank counterclockwise preferred the familiar, while people who turned it clockwise preferred the new.
post: People turned a crank either clockwise or counterclockwise. Then they chose between familiar things and new ones. People who turned the crank counterclockwise preferred the familiar, while people who turned it clockwise preferred the new.

claim: The answers fell into two related groups, one for each kind of belief.
post: Adults filled out a new questionnaire about how emotions work. Some items were about whether changing how you think can change how you feel. Others were about whether feelings just happen automatically after an event. The answers fell into two related groups, one for each kind of belief.

claim: Their science identity and their sense of belonging to STEM and to the university went up.
post: Incoming college STEM students took part in a one-week program just before their first semester. It included small-group activities, mentoring, and career planning. Students filled out surveys before and after the week. Their science identity and their sense of belonging to STEM and to the university went up.

claim: When style was ignored, the scores did not line up.
post: Patients took two personality tests: one asking what they see in inkblots, the other a questionnaire about themselves. Researchers also looked at each patient's general style of answering on each test. Patients with a similar style on both tests had distress scores that lined up strongly across the tests. When style was ignored, the scores did not line up.

claim: Their scores were higher after the training on every one.
post: Teachers attended a four-day training series spread over a year, with coaching and practice between sessions. It taught them how to figure out why a student misbehaves and build a plan around it. They answered the same questions about 15 ideas and strategies before and after. Their scores were higher after the training on every one.

claim: People who were moderately religious supported killing animals less than people who were not religious at all or very religious.
post: College students filled out questions about how religious they were. They also said how much they supported killing animals in different areas of life. People who were moderately religious supported killing animals less than people who were not religious at all or very religious.

claim: Their long-term plans matched what psychologists aim for, but their immediate responses resembled the unhelpful reactions seen in earlier studies of staff.
post: Care staff were asked about a made-up young man whose behavior was hard to handle. They described what they would do right away and what they would do over the longer term. Their long-term plans matched what psychologists aim for, but their immediate responses resembled the unhelpful reactions seen in earlier studies of staff.

claim: More people chose the premium option when its price was shown as the extra cost.
post: People chose between a basic option and a premium option, such as direct flights. For some, the premium price was shown as the extra cost, 'for $20 more'. For others it was shown as the total, 'for $60 total'. More people chose the premium option when its price was shown as the extra cost.

claim: Starting with the full task was more reliable and efficient.
post: Young children with autism learned to point to the picture that matched a spoken word. Each child learned one set of pictures by practicing the pieces separately first, and another set by practicing the full word-to-picture matching from the start. Starting with the full task was more reliable and efficient.

claim: People rated their health as better, and fewer said "fair" or "poor," when the list started with "excellent."
post: People in an online survey rated their own health as excellent, very good, good, fair, or poor. For some, the choices were listed starting with "excellent." For others, the list started with "poor." People rated their health as better, and fewer said "fair" or "poor," when the list started with "excellent."

claim: Zoo animals were rated as restricted, tame, and passive, while wild animals were rated as free, wild, and active.
post: People looked at slides of eight kinds of animals, shown in the wild, in a natural-looking zoo, or in a caged zoo. Others saw no slides. Everyone rated the animals on word scales. Zoo animals were rated as restricted, tame, and passive, while wild animals were rated as free, wild, and active.

claim: Feeling too close faded faster than feeling not close enough, and it depended less on how much contact the partners had that day.
post: Couples kept a daily diary for 12 days, noting whether they felt less close to their partner than they wanted, or more close than they wanted. Researchers tracked how those feelings changed from day to day. Feeling too close faded faster than feeling not close enough, and it depended less on how much contact the partners had that day.

claim: The gap between women and men was larger in countries with longer healthy lives, more education and more wealth than in countries with less.
post: People in 55 countries filled out a personality questionnaire that covered traits like extraversion and agreeableness. Researchers compared women's and men's answers across countries. The gap between women and men was larger in countries with longer healthy lives, more education and more wealth than in countries with less.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: Children in the US mostly picked the matching block, while children in China mostly picked the pair that fit the "different" pattern.
post: Three-year-olds watched a box that seemed to play music when certain pairs of painted blocks were placed on top. One block showed up in both pairs that worked. Then each child picked between two pairs: two matching blocks, or the two different blocks that had worked. Children in the US mostly picked the matching block, while children in China mostly picked the pair that fit the "different" pattern.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

claim: People thought women confess love first and feel happier when they hear it, but in real relationships men confessed first and felt happier hearing it.
post: People reported on their current and past romantic relationships, saying who confessed love first and how they felt when a partner said 'I love you'. People thought women confess love first and feel happier when they hear it, but in real relationships men confessed first and felt happier hearing it.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: People who wrote about a nostalgic event chose more pumps than people who wrote about an ordinary event.
post: People wrote about either a nostalgic event from their past or an ordinary one. Then they played a computer game with 30 virtual balloons. For each balloon they chose how many times to pump it, earning money per pump but losing it all if the balloon popped. People who wrote about a nostalgic event chose more pumps than people who wrote about an ordinary event.

claim: Most of the clinic children, 84%, showed an insecure bond with their mother, compared with 28% of the other children.
post: Preschoolers each spent time with their mother, were separated from her, and then were reunited. Half had been referred to a child psychiatry clinic for serious behavior problems, and half were children without behavior problems. Most of the clinic children, 84%, showed an insecure bond with their mother, compared with 28% of the other children.

claim: Intellect was linked to overall, verbal, and nonverbal intelligence about equally, but Openness was linked only to verbal intelligence.
post: People filled out a personality questionnaire that scores two close traits separately: Intellect, a taste for ideas and abstract thinking, and Openness, a taste for art and beauty. They also had their intelligence measured. Intellect was linked to overall, verbal, and nonverbal intelligence about equally, but Openness was linked only to verbal intelligence.

claim: Showing you are sexually available was judged most effective when women used it to find a short-term partner.
post: College students judged how well different ways of attracting a partner would work. The ways were judged for men and for women, and for someone after a short-term fling versus a long-term partner. Showing you are sexually available was judged most effective when women used it to find a short-term partner.
journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

claim: American students had more liberal views, started dating younger, dated more often, and were more likely to have sex with their dates than Chinese students.
post: American and Chinese college students answered a survey about dating attitudes and behaviors. American students had more liberal views, started dating younger, dated more often, and were more likely to have sex with their dates than Chinese students.

claim: In both groups, the relative's expressed emotion was linked to relapse, even after accounting for the other social and clinical factors measured.
post: Patients leaving the hospital after treatment for schizophrenia or for depression each had a close relative who was assessed for how much emotion they expressed about the patient. Nine months later, researchers checked who had relapsed. In both groups, the relative's expressed emotion was linked to relapse, even after accounting for the other social and clinical factors measured.

claim: Babies with the short version of a serotonin-related gene were more likely to show attachment patterns with more distress than babies with the long version.
post: Mothers were watched at home with their 6-month-old babies during feeding and play. Later, at 12 and 18 months, each baby was put through mild separations from the mother in a lab, and the babies' DNA was tested years afterward. Babies with the short version of a serotonin-related gene were more likely to show attachment patterns with more distress than babies with the long version.

claim: People who had repeatedly taken tests did better than people who had repeatedly restudied.
post: People studied prose passages. Then some repeatedly restudied the material and others repeatedly took tests on it. One week later everyone took a final test with new questions that required drawing inferences. People who had repeatedly taken tests did better than people who had repeatedly restudied.
journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition

claim: Fitting that idea better went with fewer depressive symptoms, and the link was strongest for people with the A/A version of a serotonin receptor gene.
post: Adults in a Brazilian city described their own families, which were compared with a shared idea of a typical family. They also gave DNA and were followed for two years. Fitting that idea better went with fewer depressive symptoms, and the link was strongest for people with the A/A version of a serotonin receptor gene.

claim: People who were more mindful had higher pain thresholds than people who were less mindful, meaning it took more to make something hurt.
post: People who had never tried meditation were measured on how mindful they are in everyday life. They also had their sensitivity to pain measured. People who were more mindful had higher pain thresholds than people who were less mindful, meaning it took more to make something hurt.

claim: For mothers, how personality related to parenting depended on income and education; for fathers, it depended on childhood hardships.
post: Parents answered online questions about their personality, their income and education, hard experiences from their own childhood, and how they treat their child. Mothers and fathers were analyzed separately. For mothers, how personality related to parenting depended on income and education; for fathers, it depended on childhood hardships.

claim: High blood pressure was more common in both PTSD groups than in the depression-only group or the group with no mental disorder.
post: Adults in a large national survey were sorted into four groups: those who had ever had PTSD but not depression, both, depression only, or neither. Researchers then compared how many in each group had high blood pressure. High blood pressure was more common in both PTSD groups than in the depression-only group or the group with no mental disorder.

claim: Over the following months, the sleep program group had fewer insomnia symptoms and drank less than the education group.
post: Heavy drinkers who also had trouble sleeping were randomly given one of two online programs. One was a self-paced program that teaches skills for better sleep. The other was a general health education program. Over the following months, the sleep program group had fewer insomnia symptoms and drank less than the education group.

claim: The children told apart milder and more serious problems in a way that closely matched the clinicians.
post: Boys and girls in different grades were asked about peers whose behavior mental health professionals would see as signs of emotional disturbance. Their answers were compared with the judgments of clinicians. The children told apart milder and more serious problems in a way that closely matched the clinicians.

claim: People who held a hand in ice water felt less guilty afterward, and the drop was bigger than for the warm-water group.
post: People wrote about a time they treated someone badly. Then some put a hand in a bucket of ice water, and others put a hand in warm water while moving paper clips between boxes. People who held a hand in ice water felt less guilty afterward, and the drop was bigger than for the warm-water group.
